# Tangled protocol v1

Canonical specification. This is not a live network.



---

# 00-abstract.md

---
title: Abstract
slug: abstract
order: 0
---

# Abstract

Tangled is a content-network protocol. An identity is a Solana Ed25519 public key. Content lives in a signed Merkle repository on a host the identity controls (a **knot**). Authorization is object-capability. Confidentiality is encryption. Discovery and moderation are unprivileged overlays. Other networks bind in with provenance, they do not define the data model.

This document set is the implementable specification of Tangled version 1. Normative language follows [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174), as restated in [Conformance](./02-conformance.md). Every acronym used in these documents is defined in [Terminology](./01-terminology.md).

## What Tangled is

A **substrate**. Records, blobs, graphs, and media are first-class. Microblogs, long-form publishing, private groups, and datasets are applications on top of one data plane. The protocol does not privilege a social-network shape.

A **self-certifying store**. A knot is a convenient place to keep bytes. It is not an authority over identity, history, or meaning. Any replica of a repository can be verified from the signatures and the Merkle root.

A **self-hosting unit**. One process and a local database is enough to exist on the network. Global indexes (looms) and foreign-protocol facades (gateways) are optional.

## What Tangled is not

- Not a blockchain. Records are not sequenced by a global ledger. Solana keys and signatures are the identity and authenticity primitive; optional `did:sol` on-chain persistence is a transparency log, not a requirement to exist.
- Not a message bus. Followers pull. Knots do not fan out inbox POSTs.
- Not a permissioned-data fork. Public, capability-gated, and sealed records share one repository and one sync protocol. Visibility is a field on the record.
- Not a live network in this repository. This repository specifies the protocol and presents it. It does not run knots.

## Claims, and the tradeoffs they refuse

| Claim | What it refuses |
| --- | --- |
| Identity is a Solana key, rotatable in-repo | Nostr’s un-rotatable key; AT Protocol’s PLC directory as a gate |
| One data plane | AT Protocol’s split into a public Merkle Search Tree (MST) protocol and a separate permissioned protocol that provides “access control, not confidentiality” |
| Capabilities gate fetch; encryption gates read | ActivityPub addressing that implementations ignore; AT Protocol permissioned data that the host can read |
| Pull sync of a Merkle tree | ActivityPub N² delivery; Nostr full-event flood as the only sync |
| Looms are unprivileged | AT Protocol relays and AppViews as required infrastructure |
| Gateways with provenance | One-off bridges that cannot round-trip |

Honest losses, stated here so the rest of the spec does not have to apologize for them: Tangled has no incumbent graph. Private records cannot be globally indexed. Capability revocation needs a time-to-live (TTL) or an online check. Human handles lean on the Domain Name System (DNS) or Solana Name Service (SNS). ActivityPub (AP) imports are gateway-attested because AP objects are not author-signed.

# 01-terminology.md

title: Terminology

# Terminology

This page defines every acronym used in the Tangled specification and the protocol nouns that those documents rely on. Prose MUST expand an acronym on first use in each document and MUST have a row here.

Protocol nouns (knot, repo, circle) are in [Glossary](#glossary). Acronyms are in [Acronyms](#acronyms).

## Acronyms

| Acronym | Expansion | Meaning in Tangled | See |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AEAD | Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data | Symmetric encryption of record bodies under an epoch secret or Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) context. | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| ACL | Access Control List | Informal name for the capability system. Tangled does not store a central who-can-do-what table; it verifies capability chains. | [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md) |
| AP | ActivityPub | W3C federated social protocol. Tangled gateways MAY speak AP. AP objects are not author-signed; imports are gateway-attested. | [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md) |
| API | Application Programming Interface | The Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) methods a knot exposes. | [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md) |
| ASCII | American Standard Code for Information Interchange | Restricted character set used in the Solana off-chain signing envelope when the digest is hex-encoded. | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| ATProto | Authenticated Transfer Protocol | Bluesky’s protocol. Compared in this spec; a gateway MAY speak a subset of its XRPC methods. | [Comparison](./19-comparison.md) |
| BLAKE3 | BLAKE3 hash function | The only content hash. 256-bit digest. | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| C2S | Client-to-Server | ActivityPub client API. A gateway MAY expose C2S as a facade over the local repo. | [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md) |
| CAR | Content Addressable aRchive | IPLD file format used to export and sync repositories. | [Synchronization](./11-sync.md) |
| CBOR | Concise Binary Object Representation | Binary encoding. Tangled uses DAG-CBOR, the canonical IPLD profile of CBOR. | [Data model](./06-data-model.md) |
| CDDL | Concise Data Definition Language | Schema language for CBOR types in `spec/cddl/`. | [Data model](./06-data-model.md) |
| CID | Content Identifier | CIDv1 naming a DAG-CBOR block hashed with BLAKE3-256. | [Data model](./06-data-model.md) |
| CRDT | Conflict-free Replicated Data Type | Not used in version 1. Concurrent same-key writes use Last-ts-wins among causal heads, with optional merge records. | [Data model](./06-data-model.md) |
| DAG | Directed Acyclic Graph | IPLD linking: blocks point at other blocks by CID. Repositories are DAGs. | [Repositories](./07-repositories.md) |
| DAG-CBOR | DAG profile of CBOR | Canonical CBOR used on the wire and as the input to BLAKE3. | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| DHKEM | Diffie–Hellman Key Encapsulation Mechanism | HPKE KEM. Tangled uses DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256). | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| DID | Decentralized Identifier | `did:sol:<base58-pubkey>`. Generative by default. | [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md) |
| DNS | Domain Name System | One handle type: TXT at `_tangled.<domain>` or HTTPS well-known. | [Resolution](./13-resolution.md) |
| DoS | Denial of Service | Threat class, including forced-upgrade by spam-adding circle members. | [Threat model](./18-threat-model.md) |
| E2EE | End-to-End Encryption | Sealed records: the knot stores ciphertext. Distinct from capability gating. | [Visibility](./08-visibility.md) |
| Ed25519 | Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm, 25519 | Solana’s signature scheme. Identity keys and record signatures. | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| FID | Farcaster ID | Numeric on-chain identity in Farcaster. Bindable via `sys/binding`. | [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md) |
| HKDF | HMAC-based Key Derivation Function | Used inside HPKE and to derive application keys from an epoch secret. | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| HMAC | Hash-based Message Authentication Code | Building block of HKDF. | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| HPKE | Hybrid Public Key Encryption | RFC 9180. 1:1 sealed records and small-group epoch-secret wraps. | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| HTTP | Hypertext Transfer Protocol | Transport for the knot API. HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. | [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md) |
| HTTPS | HTTP Secure | HTTP over Transport Layer Security (TLS). Required for production knots. | [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md) |
| IPLD | InterPlanetary Linked Data | Content-addressed data model. CID, DAG-CBOR, CAR. | [Data model](./06-data-model.md) |
| IRI | Internationalized Resource Identifier | RFC 3987. ActivityPub object `id` values are IRIs; the canonical `foreign_id` for `activitypub` is that `id`. | [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md) |
| JSON | JavaScript Object Notation | Debug and HTTP mapping of DAG-CBOR. Not canonical for hashing. | [Data model](./06-data-model.md) |
| JWT | JSON Web Token | Not used. Capabilities are DAG-CBOR UCAN-profile certificates, not JWTs. | [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md) |
| KEM | Key Encapsulation Mechanism | HPKE primitive. See DHKEM. | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| MLS | Messaging Layer Security | RFC 9420. Large-group distributor of the circle epoch secret. Version 1 required for group-capable implementations. | [Circles](./10-circles.md) |
| MST | Merkle Search Tree | Ordered Merkle tree keyed by `collection/rkey`. Repository data structure. | [Repositories](./07-repositories.md) |
| NIP | Nostr Implementation Possibility | Nostr extension documents. Cited where Tangled maps kinds. | [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md) |
| OpenAPI | OpenAPI Specification | Machine-readable HTTP API in `spec/http/openapi.yaml`. | [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md) |
| PDS | Personal Data Server | AT Protocol name for a user host. A Tangled knot is the analogous unit, not a PDS. | [Comparison](./19-comparison.md) |
| PLC | Public Ledger of Credentials | AT Protocol DID method (`did:plc`) and its directory. Tangled does not use PLC. | [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md) |
| RFC | Request for Comments | IETF documents. Tangled profiles RFC 2119, 8174, 8949, 9180, 9420. | [Conformance](./02-conformance.md) |
| RPC | Remote Procedure Call | Knot methods are HTTP RPCs in the `tangled.*` namespace. | [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md) |
| S2S | Server-to-Server | ActivityPub federation. A gateway MAY speak S2S. | [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md) |
| SHA-256 | Secure Hash Algorithm 256-bit | Used inside HKDF-SHA256 and MLS. Not the content hash (that is BLAKE3). | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| SIWS | Sign In With Solana | Human session login to a knot. Not used to sign records. | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| SNS | Solana Name Service | On-chain name → pubkey mapping. An optional handle type. | [Resolution](./13-resolution.md) |
| SQLite | SQLite database | Recommended local store for a self-hosted knot. Not a wire requirement. | [Architecture](./03-architecture.md) |
| TCB | Trusted Computing Base | Identity, signatures, and encryption are in the TCB. Looms and gateways are not. | [Architecture](./03-architecture.md) |
| TLS | Transport Layer Security | Required for production HTTPS. | [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md) |
| TTL | Time To Live | Capability expiry and dual-stack max-skew. Offline capability checks rely on TTL. | [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md) |
| UCAN | User Controlled Authorization Network | Capability certificate family. Tangled profiles UCAN; it does not use JWT-UCAN as the wire format. | [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md) |
| URI | Uniform Resource Identifier | Handles, DIDs, collection names, HTTP endpoints. | [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md) |
| URL | Uniform Resource Locator | A URI that locates a knot or well-known resource. | [Resolution](./13-resolution.md) |
| UTF-8 | Unicode Transformation Format, 8-bit | Text encoding for JSON mappings and UTF-8 off-chain messages. | [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md) |
| UUID | Universally Unique Identifier | Not required. Record keys (`rkey`) are TID-like or caller-chosen. | [Data model](./06-data-model.md) |
| W3C | World Wide Web Consortium | Publisher of DID Core, ActivityPub, and HTTP Message Signatures. | [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md) |
| X25519 | X25519 Diffie–Hellman | Key-agreement curve. Listed separately in `sys/id`; not derived from the Ed25519 identity key for ECDH. | [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md) |
| XRPC | AT Protocol HTTP RPC style | Method names like `com.atproto.repo.getRecord`. Tangled uses `tangled.*`. Gateways MAY speak a subset of XRPC. | [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md) |
| YAML | YAML Ain’t Markup Language | Translation tables in `spec/interop/`. | [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md) |
| BIP | Bitcoin Improvement Proposal | BIP-340 is the Schnorr signature used on Nostr bindings. | [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md) |
| CORS | Cross-Origin Resource Sharing | Public knot reads MUST be CORS-open. Authorized methods MUST NOT use `*`. | [HTTP API](./12-http-api.md) |
| GC | Garbage Collection | Knots MAY GC blob bytes after a delete; tombstones remain. | [Data model](./06-data-model.md) |
| QR | Quick Response code | Out-of-band way to learn a knot URL. | [Resolution](./13-resolution.md) |
| UI | User Interface | Clients MUST NOT expose HPKE vs MLS in UI. | [Circles](./10-circles.md) |
| WebCrypto | Web Cryptography API | Browsers MAY keep device keys non-extractable. | [Migration](./17-migration.md) |

## Glossary

**Annotation pattern.** A member writes a sealed record in their own repository, encrypted to a circle, with envelope `circle` set and optional `ref` pointing at a target CID. Default write pattern for social applications. Fetch uses a membership grant (`circle/read`).

**Attested.** A claim whose authenticity rests on a gateway or host, not on the original author’s signature. ActivityPub imports are attested.

**Backlink index.** A knot-local or loom index of public records keyed by envelope `ref` (or body `reply`). Exposed as `tangled.sync.queryBacklinks` and `tangled.loom.query?type=ref`. Not a global inbox.

**Blob.** Opaque bytes addressed by CID, stored beside the repository. Media, CAR segments, ciphertext payloads larger than a record.

**Canonical foreign_id.** The protocol-defined identifier of a foreign object (Nostr event id, AT strong URI, ActivityPub `id` IRI, Farcaster message hash). The `sys.foreign` rkey is derived from `protocol` plus this value.

**Capability (cap).** A delegable, attenuable, expiring certificate that authorizes a command on a resource. Presented to a knot to fetch `vis: cap` or `vis: sealed` bytes.

**Circle.** A group with membership and a read/write policy. User operations are create, add member, remove member, send, leave. The cryptographic distributor (HPKE wrap vs MLS) is not a user-facing mode.

**Circle-scoped record.** A record whose envelope `circle` field is set. `vis` MUST be `sealed`. Fetch MAY be authorized by `circle/read` on that circle.

**Collection.** A named prefix in a repository, written as a reverse-DNS type such as `pub.tangled.post` or `sys/id`.

**Commit.** A signed snapshot of a repository: DID, MST root CID, revision, previous commit CID, Solana signature.

**Device key.** A Solana keypair that is not the identity key, authorized by a capability to sign on behalf of the identity for a limited command set.

**Distributor.** The mechanism that delivers `epoch_secret[N]` to circle members: HPKE wrap (small-group) or MLS exporter (large-group). Chosen automatically.

**Dual-stack epoch.** The single transition epoch after HPKE→MLS grow during which the new epoch secret is available both as an MLS exporter secret and as HPKE wraps, so offline members keep reading.

**Epoch secret.** A symmetric key that Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) uses for circle application payloads at epoch `N`.

**Fiber.** Informal name for a capability. Normative text says **capability**.

**Foreign binding.** A `sys/binding` record that proves a Tangled identity controls (or is attested as) an identity on another network.

**Gateway.** A knot that also speaks a foreign protocol and stores translations as `sys/foreign` envelopes.

**Generative DID.** A `did:sol` that has no on-chain document. The identifier is the public key. Default.

**Handle.** A human-readable name bidirectionally bound to a DID: a DNS name or an SNS name.

**Head.** The latest commit CID of a repository, as advertised by a knot.

**History share.** Circle policy that, on add-member, also wraps prior epoch secrets to the new member. Off by default. Not a side effect of size migration.

**Identity key.** The Solana Ed25519 keypair that *is* the account.

**Invocation.** A request signed by a capability’s audience, carrying the proof chain.

**Knot.** The host process. Serves repositories and blobs. Self-hostable as one process and a local database.

**Label.** A signed record asserting a classification of another record or DID. Clients compose labelers. Knots are not the moderation authority.

**Last-ts-wins.** Version 1 merge rule: among same-key causal heads, later `ts` is live; CID tie-break. A merge record lists concurrent heads in `prev`. Not a CRDT.

**Loom.** Optional indexer of public heads. Not in the Trusted Computing Base (TCB).

**Membership grant.** A `circle/read` capability the circle owner issues to a member DID. Revoked on remove. Independent of knot URL.

**Record.** A typed, content-addressed object signed by a Solana key, stored in a repository.

**Repo (repository).** One identity’s signed MST plus its blobs.

**rkey.** The record key inside a collection. Unique per collection per repo.

**Sealed.** Visibility class: the body is ciphertext. The knot stores opaque bytes.

**Shared-repo pattern.** A dedicated circle DID owns an MST; members hold `repo/write` capabilities and sign as device keys (`author` is the circle DID). The hosting knot signs commits. Used for wikis and datasets.

**Strand.** Informal name for a repository. Normative text says **repo**.

**Threshold.** Spec constant `CIRCLE_MLS_THRESHOLD = 16`. The member count at which a circle that has never used MLS MUST migrate to MLS. Not a client setting.

**TID.** Timestamp identifier. A sortable `rkey` derived from time plus entropy. Recommended, not required.

**Unsigned record.** The DAG-CBOR map of a record with the `sig` field omitted. Input to BLAKE3 for the signing envelope.

**Visibility (`vis`).** Record field: `public`, `cap`, or `sealed`.

**Welcome.** MLS message that introduces a member to a group. Published as a sealed record in the circle log.

**Yarn.** Informal name for a schema document. Normative text says **schema**.

# 02-conformance.md

---
title: Conformance
slug: conformance
order: 2
---

# Conformance

The key words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **REQUIRED**, **SHALL**, **SHALL NOT**, **SHOULD**, **SHOULD NOT**, **RECOMMENDED**, **NOT RECOMMENDED**, **MAY**, and **OPTIONAL** in this document set are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174) when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

## Version

This is Tangled version **1**. The integer `v` on records, commits, and capabilities is `1`. A future version MUST increment `v` and MUST define compatibility with version 1.

## Profiles

An implementation advertises a profile. Profiles are additive. Advertising a profile means the implementation implements every MUST in that profile.

| Profile | Who | MUST implement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `knot.public` | Any knot | Identity, public records, MST, pull sync, HTTP API for public methods including `tangled.sync.getBlob` for publicly referenced blobs, handle resolution. SHOULD implement `tangled.sync.queryBacklinks` from locally stored public records |
| `knot.cap` | Knots that serve `vis: cap` | Capability verification, revocation fetch or TTL, authorized sync, authorized `getBlob` |
| `knot.sealed` | Knots that store sealed records | Opaque blob storage, encrypted rkeys, no plaintext logging of bodies, `circle/read` for circle-scoped records they store |
| `knot.group` | Knots that host circles | Both Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) small-group and Messaging Layer Security (MLS) large-group distributors, seamless migration, membership grants, honor `circle/read` |
| `client.verify` | Any client | Signature verification, MST proofs, DID and handle resolution |
| `client.group` | Clients that join circles | Both distributors, dual-stack catch-up, never-downgrade |
| `gateway.ap` | Optional | ActivityPub C2S/S2S facade, attested imports labeled as such |
| `gateway.nostr` | Optional | Nostr NIP-01 relay mapping |
| `gateway.atproto` | Optional | AT Protocol XRPC subset over the same MST |

A knot that only hosts public repositories MAY omit `knot.cap`, `knot.sealed`, and `knot.group`. It MUST advertise the omission in node capabilities ([HTTP API](./12-http-api.md#tangled-node-describe)).

A `client.group` implementation MUST NOT expose Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) versus Messaging Layer Security (MLS) as a user-facing mode, setting, or prompt.

## Node capabilities document

`GET /xrpc/tangled.node.describe` returns:

```json
{
  "v": 1,
  "did": "did:sol:…",
  "profiles": ["knot.public", "knot.cap"],
  "protocols": [],
  "maxBlob": 134217728
}
```

`protocols` lists foreign facades this knot speaks (`activitypub`, `nostr`, `atproto`). Empty means none. `maxBlob` is bytes.

## Conformance tests

An implementation claiming a profile MUST pass the vectors in `spec/vectors/` that the profile lists:

| Vector file | Profiles |
| --- | --- |
| `unsigned-record.json` | `client.verify`, `knot.public` |
| `solana-signature.json` | `client.verify`, `knot.public` |
| `mst-proof.json` | `client.verify`, `knot.public` |
| `capability-chain.json` | `knot.cap`, `client.verify` |
| `hpke-sealed.json` | `knot.sealed`, `client.group` |
| `mls-welcome-commit.json` | `knot.group`, `client.group` |
| `circle-grow-dual-stack.json` | `knot.group`, `client.group` |
| `handle-dns.json` | `knot.public`, `client.verify` |
| `binding-nostr.json` | `gateway.nostr` or any client that consumes bindings |
| `circle-read-auth.json` | `knot.group`, `knot.sealed`, `client.verify` |
| `getblob-auth.json` | `knot.public`, `knot.cap`, `knot.sealed` |

Passing means: given the inputs, the implementation produces the stated digests, accepts the stated signatures, and rejects the stated negative cases.

## Extensibility

Unknown record types MUST be stored and synced if the record is well-formed (valid CID, valid signature, known `v`). Knots MUST NOT drop unknown `type` values on public collections. Clients MUST ignore unknown fields when the CDDL `any` / extra-map rule allows them.

New HTTP methods MUST live under `tangled.*` or an application namespace. Knots MUST return `MethodNotImplemented` for unknown `tangled.*` methods rather than a generic 404 that hides whether the knot is a Tangled knot.

## Normative references

Implementations MUST follow the profiles of:

- RFC 8949 (CBOR) as constrained by the DAG-CBOR canonicalization in [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md)
- RFC 9180 (HPKE) with the ciphersuite in that chapter
- RFC 9420 (MLS) with ciphersuite `0x0001` for `knot.group` / `client.group`
- [did:sol method](https://identity-com.github.io/sol-did/did-method-spec.html) generative profile
- [Solana off-chain message format](https://docs.anza.xyz/cli/examples/sign-offchain-message)
- UCAN delegation semantics as profiled in [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md)


---

# 03-architecture.md

---
title: Architecture
slug: architecture
order: 3
---

# Architecture

Tangled separates **who you are**, **what you wrote**, **who may fetch it**, **who may read it**, and **who helps you find it**. Those are different jobs. Incumbent protocols fuse them, then pay for the fusion.

## Actors

```
  Wallet ──sign──► Knot A (repo + blobs)
                      ▲
                      │ Merkle pull
                      │
                   Knot B
                      │
                      ▼
              Loom (optional index of public heads)
                      │
              Gateway knot ──translate──► ActivityPub / Nostr / AT Protocol
```

**Identity** is a Solana Ed25519 public key. A wallet holds it. See [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md).

**Knot** is the host. It stores one or more repositories and their blobs. It answers HTTP. It is cheap to self-host: one process, one local database (SQLite is RECOMMENDED, not required). A provider MAY host many identities on one knot. The knot is not the identity. If the knot lies, signatures and Merkle proofs detect it. If the knot disappears, the repository CAR moves to another knot.

**Repo** is one identity’s signed Merkle Search Tree (MST) plus blobs. The identity’s `sys/id` record lives here.

**Record** is a typed object in the MST, signed by a Solana key.

**Capability** is a certificate that authorizes a command on a resource. Knots that advertise `knot.cap` verify capabilities before serving non-public bytes.

**Circle** is a group. Members share an epoch secret. Users add and remove members. They do not pick Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) or Messaging Layer Security (MLS).

**Loom** indexes **public** heads. Clients choose looms. A loom can censor its index; it cannot rewrite a repository. Looms are outside the Trusted Computing Base (TCB).

**Gateway** is a knot that also speaks a foreign protocol. Translations are stored as `sys/foreign` records with provenance. Gateways are outside the TCB for authenticity of ActivityPub (AP) objects (those objects are not author-signed). For Nostr and AT Protocol, the original signatures remain verifiable.

## Data plane

One repository, one sync protocol, three visibility values on the record:

| `vis` | Fetch | Read | Rebroadcast |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `public` | Anyone | Anyone | Yes |
| `cap` | Bearer of a valid capability | Anyone who fetched (host included) | No |
| `sealed` | Bearer of a valid capability | Holders of the epoch secret or HPKE recipient | No |

Authorization (who the knot serves) and confidentiality (what ciphertext reveals) are separate layers. See [Visibility](./08-visibility.md).

## Control plane

Writes are local. The author signs a record, the knot inserts it into the MST, the knot signs a new commit. Followers pull the new head and the missing blocks. There is no inbox POST to every follower. There is no required global firehose.

Live updates are an optional WebSocket subscribe on the author’s knot, capability-gated when the collection is not public.

## Trust boundaries

| Component | In the TCB? | If it is malicious |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity key / wallet | Yes | Attacker is the identity until rotation |
| Device key | Scoped | Limited to the capability’s command and TTL |
| Knot | Availability and `vis: cap` plaintext | Cannot forge public or sealed records; can withhold bytes; can read `vis: cap` |
| Replica / other knots | Availability | Same as knot for copies they hold |
| Loom | No | Can omit or rank; cannot forge |
| Gateway | No for AP; verification-only for Nostr/AT | Can lie about AP; cannot forge Nostr/AT if clients verify |
| DNS / SNS | Handle binding | Can seize the name, not the DID |
| `did:sol` on-chain document | Optional transparency | Can be withheld; generative DID still works |

## Self-hosting

A conforming `knot.public` MUST run on a single machine with:

- An HTTP server
- Storage for MST nodes, records, commits, and blobs
- The identity’s or a delegated device’s signing capability for commits it produces
- Outbound HTTP to resolve handles and to pull other repos the operator follows

It MUST NOT require a relay, a loom, a PLC directory, or an AppView to accept writes or to serve the operator’s own data to clients that know the knot URL.

## Application layer

Core collections (`sys/*`, graph, labels, circles) are specified here. Applications add collections. Unknown collections sync. Example applications (post, article, annotation, media, album, page, circle chat) are specified so the substrate is demonstrable; they are not the protocol. Worked examples: [Use cases](./20-use-cases.md).

## Why pull

ActivityPub delivers by pushing into inboxes. Cost grows with audience. Failure is silent. Tangled followers remember the author’s knot location (from `sys/id` and handle resolution) and pull the MST. Cost grows with the bytes you read. Failure is visible: the head does not move.

Nostr relays store events and let clients subscribe. There is no authoritative repository, so clients poll many relays and hope. Tangled has an authoritative signed head per identity, and any number of replicas.

AT Protocol pulls too, then inserts a relay that concatenates every public commit into a firehose so AppViews can exist. Tangled looms MAY do that for public data. They MUST NOT be required for two knots to sync.


---

# 04-identifiers.md

---
title: Identifiers
slug: identifiers
order: 4
---

# Identifiers

A Tangled identity is a Solana account: a 32-byte Ed25519 public key. Display form is Bitcoin-alphabet base58, 43 or 44 characters. Every wallet is already an identity. There is no registration. There is no on-chain rent required to exist.

## DID

The Decentralized Identifier (DID) is generative [`did:sol`](https://identity-com.github.io/sol-did/did-method-spec.html):

```
did:sol:<base58-pubkey>
```

Implementations MUST accept `did:sol:` on mainnet with no cluster prefix. Implementations MUST accept `did:sol:devnet:` and `did:sol:testnet:` when talking to those clusters. The identifier without a cluster prefix denotes mainnet-beta.

Tangled MUST NOT invent a `did:tangled` method.

A generative DID has no on-chain document. Resolution of a generative DID MUST produce a DID document whose sole verification method is the public key itself, with `capabilityInvocation` and `authentication` granted to that key.

Persisting a DID document on-chain via the `did:sol` program is OPTIONAL. When present, it is a transparency log for rotation, not a gate on existence. A knot MUST serve `sys/id` even if no on-chain document exists.

## sys/id

The repository MUST contain a record at collection `sys.id` with rkey `self` (written `sys/id` in prose). That record is the operational DID document for Tangled.

CDDL: `IdRecord` in `spec/cddl/id.cddl`.

Fields:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v` | `1` | Version |
| `pubkey` | `bstr .size 32` | Identity Ed25519 public key, raw |
| `agreement` | `bstr .size 32` | X25519 public key for Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) and Messaging Layer Security (MLS). MUST be a distinct key. Implementations MUST NOT convert the identity Ed25519 key to X25519 for Diffie–Hellman. |
| `rotation` | `[+ bstr .size 32]` | Ordered Solana public keys that may rotate the identity. Index 0 is highest priority. |
| `recovery` | `[* bstr .size 32]` | Keys that may start a recovery. Empty is allowed; losing the identity key is then permanent. |
| `endpoints` | `[+ Endpoint]` | Knot URLs. `type` is `"knot"`. First is preferred. |
| `alsoKnownAs` | `[* text]` | Handles this DID claims: DNS names and SNS names. |
| `bindings` | `[* cid]` | CIDs of `sys/binding` records. |
| `headHint` | `cid` (optional) | Last commit CID this identity published, for stale-head detection. |

The record is signed like any other record, by the current identity key or by a rotation key during a rotation commit.

Clients MUST cache the latest `sys/id` CID they have verified. A knot that serves an older `sys/id` is stale or hostile. Clients SHOULD compare `headHint` and the served commit head.

## Handles

A handle is a human-readable name bound to a DID. Two types:

1. **DNS.** A hostname such as `alice.example.com`. Proof is either:
   - A DNS TXT record at `_tangled.<hostname>` whose value is the DID, or
   - `https://<hostname>/.well-known/tangled-did` serving `text/plain` with the DID as the sole line, or JSON `{"did":"did:sol:…"}`.
2. **SNS.** A Solana Name Service domain. Proof is the SNS record whose owner or specified Tangled field is the identity public key. Resolution procedure is in [Resolution](./13-resolution.md).

Bidirectional binding: `sys/id.alsoKnownAs` MUST list the handle, and the handle proof MUST name the DID. Clients MUST reject one-sided claims.

A DID MAY have zero handles. A DID MAY have several. The DID is the stable identifier; the handle is a pointer.

## Rotation

Three procedures. Implementations MUST NOT conflate them.

### Device-key-only

Revoke the old device capability; issue a new `repo/write` (and related) capability to the new device public key. `sys/id.pubkey` and `sys/id.agreement` MUST NOT change. Circle epoch secrets MUST NOT be re-wrapped. See [Circles](./10-circles.md#device-key-only-rotation).

### Agreement-only

The X25519 `agreement` key is compromised or rotated on a schedule; the identity Ed25519 key is unchanged. Write a new `sys/id` with the new `agreement`. Sign the commit with the current identity key (no rotation commit). Then follow [Circles](./10-circles.md#agreement-rotation): the rotating member’s client re-wraps epoch secrets and, when the distributor is MLS, publishes an MLS Update.

### Identity key (and agreement)

To rotate the identity key:

1. Produce a new Ed25519 keypair and a new X25519 agreement key. Writers MUST rotate `agreement` whenever they rotate `pubkey`.
2. Write a new `sys/id` listing the new `pubkey`, the new `agreement`, and an updated `rotation` list that still includes a key the operator holds.
3. Sign the new repository commit with **both** the current identity key and a key from `rotation` (two signatures on the commit; see [Repositories](./07-repositories.md#rotation-commits)).
4. Optionally submit the new verification methods to the on-chain `did:sol` program.
5. Re-wrap circle epoch secrets and publish MLS Updates as specified in [Circles](./10-circles.md#agreement-rotation). The rotating member’s client MUST do this without a user-facing cryptographic mode.

The Decentralized Identifier (DID) string remains `did:sol:<original-base58>`. `sys/id.pubkey` is the current signing key. After rotation, records signed by the old key remain valid in history. New records MUST be signed by the new key. Capabilities issued by the old key remain valid until they expire or are revoked; issuers SHOULD revoke and reissue.

If the identity key is stolen and a rotation key is held:

- The operator rotates as above.
- Clients that cached the previous `sys/id` accept the rotation because it is signed by a listed rotation key.
- Clients that only know the stolen key MUST be told the new head out of band (DNS `head` TXT, SNS field, or a replica). This is the cost of having no global PLC directory.

If both identity and rotation keys are lost, the DID is unrecoverable unless a `recovery` key exists. A recovery key MAY produce a rotation commit. Knots SHOULD delay serving a recovery-only rotation for 72 hours while serving both heads, matching the recovery window idea in AT Protocol without a PLC operator.

Moving a knot (`endpoints` only) is [Migration](./17-migration.md). It MUST NOT rotate `pubkey` or `agreement`.

## Device keys

The identity key SHOULD NOT live on every laptop. A device generates its own Solana keypair. The identity issues a capability (`repo/write` attenuated to collections and a TTL) to that device public key. The device signs records with the device key. The record’s `author` remains the identity DID. The record includes `signedBy` (the device public key) and the capability CID in `proof`.

Verifiers MUST:

1. Verify the record signature against `signedBy`.
2. Verify the capability chain from the identity to `signedBy`.
3. Verify the capability authorizes the collection and has not expired or been revoked.

## Foreign identifiers

Other-network identifiers are not Tangled identities. They bind through `sys/binding` as specified in [Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md). `alsoKnownAs` MUST NOT be used as the only proof of a foreign identity.

## Comparison notes

- Nostr: the public key is the identity, but it cannot rotate. Tangled rotates.
- AT Protocol: DID plus PLC directory. Tangled uses `did:sol` generative, no directory required.
- ActivityPub: `@user@host`. The host is the identity. Tangled’s host is a location.
- Farcaster: on-chain FID plus rent. Tangled requires no rent to exist.


---

# 05-cryptography.md

---
title: Cryptography
slug: cryptography
order: 5
---

# Cryptography

Tangled reuses existing primitives. This chapter profiles them. It does not invent a signature scheme, a KEM, or a group ratchet.

## Algorithms

| Role | Algorithm | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity and record signatures | Ed25519 | Solana’s scheme. 32-byte public key, 64-byte signature |
| Content hash | BLAKE3-256 | Only content hash. SHA-256 appears only inside HKDF and MLS |
| Block identifier | CIDv1, codec `dag-cbor` (0x71), multihash `blake3` (0x1e), 32-byte digest | |
| Canonical encoding | DAG-CBOR | Input to BLAKE3. JSON is a mapping, not a hash input |
| 1:1 and small-group wrap | HPKE RFC 9180 | KEM `0x0020` DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256), KDF `0x0001` HKDF-SHA256, AEAD `0x0003` ChaCha20Poly1305 |
| Circle large-group | MLS RFC 9420 | Ciphersuite `0x0001` `MLS_128_DHKEMX25519_AES128GCM_SHA256_Ed25519` |
| Circle application AEAD | ChaCha20-Poly1305 | Key = HKDF-SHA256(`epoch_secret[N]`, info=`tangled.epoch.aead.v1`) |

Implementations MUST reject other signature schemes for Tangled records. Foreign envelopes MAY carry foreign signatures as opaque bytes.

## DAG-CBOR canonicalization

Unsigned records, commits, capabilities, and schema documents MUST hash as DAG-CBOR with:

- Major types as in RFC 8949
- Map keys as UTF-8 strings, sorted by UTF-8 byte order
- No indefinite-length items
- No tags other than CID tag `42` as specified by DAG-CBOR
- Integers in shortest form
- No duplicate map keys

JSON mapping: CIDs become `{"/":"<base32-cid>"}` (IPLD JSON). Bytes become `{"/":{"bytes":"<base64>"}}`. Implementations MUST NOT hash JSON.

## Content Identifier

```
cid = CIDv1( 0x71 dag-cbor, 0x1e blake3, 32, blake3(dag-cbor-bytes) )
```

Display: `b` multibase (base32, lowercase, no padding) unless a document says otherwise. Test vectors use this encoding.

## Solana signatures

Public keys and signatures on the wire (DAG-CBOR) are raw bytes, 32 and 64. Display is base58.

### Signing envelope

A record signature is Ed25519 over the **Solana off-chain message** whose body is the hex digest of the unsigned record. This is mandatory so a Tangled signature cannot be a valid Solana transaction, and so hardware wallets and `solana sign-offchain-message` agree.

Construct the message as:

```
header     = 0xff || "solana offchain"          ; 16 bytes
version    = 0x00                               ; 1 byte, currently the only version
format     = 0x00                               ; 1 byte, restricted ASCII
length     = uint16le(64)                       ; 2 bytes, body length
body       = lowercase_hex( BLAKE3-256( unsigned_record_dag_cbor ) )
                                                ; 64 ASCII bytes
message    = header || version || format || length || body
signature  = Ed25519.Sign(identity_or_device_sk, message)
```

`unsigned_record_dag_cbor` is the record map with `sig` omitted.

Verifiers MUST rebuild this exact byte string and call Ed25519 verify with the author’s (or `signedBy`) public key.

Wallet-adapter `signMessage` is equivalent if and only if the client passes `message` (the full envelope bytes) to the wallet. Clients MUST NOT pass only the digest or only the CBOR.

Sign In With Solana (SIWS) authenticates a human session to a knot’s HTTPS surface. SIWS MUST NOT be used as a record signature.

### Commit signatures

A commit signs the same envelope construction, with `unsigned_record_dag_cbor` replaced by the unsigned commit map (`sig` and `sigRotation` omitted). Rotation commits carry a second signature `sigRotation` over the same message, verified against a key listed in the previous `sys/id.rotation`.

## HPKE

Used for:

1. **1:1 sealed records.** The body is an HPKE seal to the recipient’s X25519 `agreement` key. Info string: `tangled.hpke.record.v1`. Associated data: the unsigned record’s DAG-CBOR without `body` and `sig`.
2. **Small-group epoch wraps.** Each member receives HPKE wrap of `epoch_secret[N]`. Info string: `tangled.hpke.epoch.v1`. Associated data: `circle_did || uint64be(N)`.

Single-shot HPKE (base mode) MUST be used. The encapsulating key (`enc`) is stored beside the ciphertext.

## MLS

Ciphersuite MUST be `0x0001`. Credential type: basic credential whose identity is the 32-byte Solana public key (not the DID string). Application ID: `tangled.circle.v1`.

The MLS **exporter secret** with label `tangled.epoch` and context `uint64be(N)` and length 32 is `epoch_secret[N]` when the distributor is MLS.

Welcome and Commit messages are stored as sealed records in the circle log (`sys.circle.mls`, rkey = TID). They are not user-visible.

Group-capable implementations MUST implement MLS. Knots that only advertise `knot.public` MAY omit it.

## Epoch application keys

```
epoch_secret[N]     : 32 bytes   (from HPKE wrap or MLS exporter)
aead_key            = HKDF-SHA256-Extract-Expand(
                        salt = "tangled.epoch.aead.v1",
                        ikm  = epoch_secret[N],
                        info = circle_did,
                        L    = 32)
nonce_base          = HKDF-SHA256-Extract-Expand(
                        salt = "tangled.epoch.nonce.v1",
                        ikm  = epoch_secret[N],
                        info = circle_did,
                        L    = 12)
```

Record AEAD nonce = `nonce_base` XOR first 12 bytes of BLAKE3(unsigned record without body). Ciphertext is ChaCha20-Poly1305 over the body bytes.

## Constants

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `CIRCLE_MLS_THRESHOLD` | 16 |
| `DUAL_STACK_MAX_SKEW_EPOCHS` | 8 |
| `DUAL_STACK_MAX_SKEW_SECONDS` | 259200 (72 hours) |
| `AGREEMENT_ROTATION_MAX_SKEW_SECONDS` | 604800 (7 days) |
| `RECOVERY_DELAY_SECONDS` | 259200 |
| `CAPABILITY_MAX_TTL_SECONDS` | 31536000 (365 days) |

Implementations MUST use these values. They MUST NOT expose them as interop-breaking settings.

## Negative requirements

- MUST NOT use the identity Ed25519 key for X25519 Diffie–Hellman.
- MUST NOT sign raw DAG-CBOR or a raw 32-byte digest without the off-chain envelope.
- MUST NOT use JWT as the capability encoding.
- MUST NOT treat SIWS as a record signature.
- MUST NOT re-encrypt history on HPKE→MLS migration.


---

# 06-data-model.md

---
title: Data model
slug: data-model
order: 6
---

# Data model

Everything a knot stores is either a **record** (a typed, signed object in the Merkle Search Tree) or a **blob** (opaque bytes addressed by CID). Schemas are records. Capabilities are records. Foreign envelopes are records.

## Record

CDDL: `Record` in `spec/cddl/record.cddl`.

```
Record v1 = {
  v: 1,
  type: cid,              ; schema CID
  collection: text,       ; e.g. "pub.tangled.post"
  rkey: text,             ; unique in (did, collection)
  author: did,            ; "did:sol:<base58>"
  ts: uint,               ; Unix milliseconds
  prev: [* cid],          ; causal parents
  vis: vis,               ; "public" / "cap" / "sealed"
  body: any / ciphertext,
  ? signedBy: bstr .size 32,
  ? proof: [* cid],       ; capability CIDs
  ? ref: cid,             ; annotation target (record CID)
  ? epoch: uint,          ; circle epoch for sealed application data
  ? circle: text,         ; did:sol:<owner>#<circle-rkey> when circle-scoped
  sig: bstr .size 64
}
```

`type` is the CID of a `sys.schema` record. Implementations MAY also match `collection` as a hint; verification is against `type`.

`rkey` MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9._~:!-]{1,256}`. A timestamp identifier (TID) is RECOMMENDED: 13-character Crockford base32 of `(unix_micros << 10) | entropy10`. Nested wiki slugs for `pub.tangled.page` are specified in [Page slugs](#page-slugs).

`prev` lists CIDs of **same-key** causal parents: records that share this record’s `(author, collection, rkey)`. Empty means a root. Cross-record replies and annotations MUST use envelope `ref` (and MAY repeat the target in the application body as `reply`); they MUST NOT use `prev` for a different rkey. Concurrent writes are resolved by **Last-ts-wins among causal heads** ([Merge rule](#merge-rule-last-ts-wins)).

`signedBy` and `proof` are REQUIRED when the signer is a device key. They MUST be absent when the identity key signs.

`ref` is the CID of the record this record annotates or replies to at the envelope layer. Application bodies MAY also carry `reply` (a record CID). Clients assembling threads MUST treat `ref` as authoritative when both are present and MUST reject a public record whose `reply` CID disagrees with `ref`.

`circle` marks a **circle-scoped** record. If `circle` is present:

- `vis` MUST be `sealed`
- the value MUST be `did:sol:<owner>#<circle-rkey>` identifying a `sys.circle` record
- after decrypt, if the application body contains a `circle` field, it MUST equal the envelope value; clients MUST discard a mismatch
- fetch MAY be authorized by `circle/read` on that circle, not only by `repo/read` on this author ([Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md), [Circles](./10-circles.md#membership-grant))

The record CID is BLAKE3 of the **complete** DAG-CBOR including `sig`. The unsigned map (no `sig`) is the signing input as specified in [Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md).

## Visibility

`vis` is defined in [Visibility](./08-visibility.md). Summary:

- `public` — body is plaintext DAG-CBOR of the application value.
- `cap` — body is plaintext; the knot serves it only with a capability.
- `sealed` — body is a `Ciphertext` map.

## Ciphertext

```
Ciphertext = {
  alg: "hpke-record" / "epoch-aead",
  ? enc: bstr,            ; HPKE encapsulating key
  ? recipients: [* { kid: bstr, enc: bstr, ct: bstr }],
  ct: bstr,               ; ciphertext + tag
  ? epoch: uint
}
```

`alg = "hpke-record"` is 1:1 HPKE. `alg = "epoch-aead"` is circle AEAD under `epoch_secret[epoch]`.

## Blobs

A blob is raw bytes. Its CID uses codec `raw` (0x55) and BLAKE3-256. Maximum size is the knot’s `maxBlob` (MUST be at least 1 MiB, SHOULD be at least 128 MiB).

Records reference blobs by CID. Knots MUST NOT infer a blob’s meaning from its bytes. Sealed records MAY store ciphertext as a blob and keep a small `Ciphertext` header in the record with `ct` omitted and `blob: cid` set. For sealed media, the blob bytes MUST be ciphertext, not plaintext. Fetch is `tangled.sync.getBlob` ([Synchronization](./11-sync.md#get-blob)).

## Schemas

Collection `sys.schema`, rkey = TID. Body:

```
Schema = {
  v: 1,
  name: text,             ; "pub.tangled.post"
  fields: any,            ; JSON Schema 2020-12 object describing the body
  ? cddl: text            ; optional CDDL for the body
}
```

The schema’s CID is `type` on instance records. Evolving a schema means publishing a new schema record (new CID). Old records keep the old `type`. Compatibility maps are OPTIONAL application data, not a protocol concern.

Core schemas in `spec/schemas/` are frozen for version 1. Applications add schemas as records; they do not need a registry.

## Core collections

| Collection | rkey | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sys.id` | `self` | DID document |
| `sys.schema` | TID | Schemas |
| `sys.revocation` | capability CID (base32) | Revocations |
| `sys.binding` | TID | Foreign identity bindings |
| `sys.foreign` | TID | Foreign object envelopes |
| `sys.circle` | circle TID | Circle definition |
| `sys.circle.mls` | TID | MLS Welcome/Commit |
| `sys.circle.wrap` | `{epoch}-{member-base58}` | HPKE wraps of epoch secrets |
| `tangled.graph.follow` | target DID (safe) | Follow |
| `tangled.graph.block` | target DID (safe) | Block |
| `tangled.label` | TID | Labels |
| `tangled.blobref` | blob CID (base32) | Optional metadata for a blob |

“Safe” DID rkey: replace `:` with `.` so `did.sol.<base58>`.

A follow record MAY include `knot` (the target’s knot URL) so first-time clients can resolve without a directory. Clients MUST still verify `sys/id` at that URL.

## Example application collections

Informative, fully specified in `spec/schemas/`:

| Collection | Body gist |
| --- | --- |
| `pub.tangled.post` | `text` (≤ 32 KiB), `langs`, optional `reply` (parent record CID), optional `media` CIDs |
| `pub.tangled.article` | `title`, optional `text` preview, optional canonical `blob`, `langs`, optional `media` CIDs |
| `pub.tangled.annotation` | `text`, optional `quote` span, optional `media`; envelope `ref` MUST be the target record CID |
| `pub.tangled.media` | `blob`, `alt`, `mime` |
| `pub.tangled.album` | `title`, `items` (CIDs of `pub.tangled.media` records) |
| `pub.tangled.page` | wiki page: `title`, `text` and/or `blob`; rkey is the slug encoded as in [Page slugs](#page-slugs) |
| `pub.tangled.chat` | sealed circle message: `text` or blob; body `circle` MUST equal envelope `circle` |

These exist so a substrate is not a secret microblog. Conforming knots MUST sync them like any collection. Conforming clients need not implement their UI. When `pub.tangled.article.blob` is set, clients MUST treat that blob as the canonical body; `text` is a preview.

## Merge rule (Last-ts-wins)

Version 1 does **not** specify a Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT). The merge rule for records that share `(author, collection, rkey)` is **Last-ts-wins among causal heads**:

1. Record B **supersedes** record A when they share `(author, collection, rkey)` and A’s CID appears in B’s `prev`, or in the `prev` of a same-key ancestor of B.
2. A **causal head** is a same-key record that is not superseded.
3. The **live** record is the causal head with the greatest `ts`. If `ts` is equal, the lexicographically greatest record CID wins (CID compared as multibase base32 text).
4. A **merge record** is a same-key record whose `prev` lists two or more causal heads. Writing one is OPTIONAL. A client that merges concurrent edits MUST include every concurrent head it considered in `prev`. The body is the author’s merged value. There is no automatic field-wise merge.
5. If no merge record exists, step 3 picks one concurrent head. The loser remains in the Merkle Search Tree (MST) until a delete tombstone or a later merge record `prev`s it.
6. A delete (`body` `null`) is an ordinary record under this rule: its `prev` SHOULD list every causal head being deleted.

Implementations MUST apply this rule for `pub.tangled.page` and for any other same-key edit. Clients MUST NOT invent a CRDT for v1.

## Page slugs

`pub.tangled.page` uses `rkey` as the page slug. The rkey charset forbids `/`, so nested pages use `.` as the path separator.

**Encoding (normative):**

- A slug is a sequence of one or more **segments** joined by `.`.
- Each segment MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9_~:!-]+` (the rkey charset minus `.`) and MUST be at least one character.
- The complete rkey MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9._~:!-]{1,256}` and MUST NOT start with `.`, end with `.`, or contain `..`.
- There is no percent-encoding. Characters outside the segment charset MUST NOT appear in the rkey; they belong in the page `title`.
- `.` in the rkey is only a path separator. A single-segment page MUST NOT include `.` (put punctuation in `title`).

**Display (normative):** clients presenting a wiki hierarchy MUST render slug `a.b.c` as `a/b/c`. The stored rkey remains `a.b.c`. Example: rkey `rfc.draft` is the page `rfc/draft`; rkey `Home` is the page `Home`.

## Deletes

A delete is a record with the same `collection` and `rkey`, `body` `null`, `prev` listing the CIDs being deleted, and a new `sig`. Public deletes are tombstones in the MST. Sealed deletes MUST be indistinguishable from other sealed records at the knot (same size class); the body ciphertext decrypts to `null`.

Knots MAY garbage-collect blob bytes after a delete. They MUST keep the tombstone so sync converges.


---

# 07-repositories.md

---
title: Repositories
slug: repositories
order: 7
---

# Repositories

A repository is a signed Merkle Search Tree (MST) of records plus a blob store. The MST is the same idea as AT Protocol’s repository: keys are `collection/rkey`, values are record CIDs, interior nodes are content-addressed. Tangled uses BLAKE3 and DAG-CBOR instead of SHA-256 and DAG-CBOR-with-sha256.

Partial sync and inclusion proofs are why MST is used for **all** visibility classes, including sealed collections. AT Protocol’s permissioned-data proposal abandons MST for a set hash because “partial sync is less important.” Tangled keeps one code path.

## Keys

MST key = UTF-8 `collection + "/" + rkey`. Keys MUST be unique. Keys MUST NOT contain `0x00`.

## Node structure

Fanout is 4 bits (16-way), as in AT Protocol. A node is:

```
MstNode = {
  l: cid / null,          ; left subtree for keys before this node’s first entry
  e: [+ MstEntry]
}

MstEntry = {
  p: uint,                ; prefix length shared with previous key
  k: bstr,                ; key suffix
  v: cid,                 ; record CID
  t: cid / null           ; right subtree
}
```

Empty repository: no nodes; the data CID on the commit is the CID of an empty node `{l: null, e: []}`.

Implementations MUST produce the same node CID as `spec/vectors/mst-proof.json` for the listed insertions.

## Commit

```
Commit = {
  v: 1,
  did: did,
  data: cid,              ; MST root
  rev: text,              ; TID, monotonically increasing
  prev: cid / null,
  sig: bstr .size 64,
  ? sigRotation: bstr .size 64
}
```

`rev` MUST be greater (TID order) than `prev`’s commit `rev` when `prev` is not null.

The commit CID is BLAKE3 of the complete DAG-CBOR including signatures. The signing envelope hashes the unsigned commit ([Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md#commit-signatures)).

A knot advertises **head** = latest commit CID for a DID.

## Rotation commits

When `sys/id` changes `pubkey`, the commit MUST include `sigRotation` verifiable with a key listed in the **previous** `sys/id.rotation`. Verifiers MUST:

1. Load previous `sys/id` from `prev` commit’s MST.
2. Verify `sig` with the new `pubkey` (the new identity signs its own first commit).
3. Verify `sigRotation` with a previous rotation key.

Recovery commits (signed by `recovery` instead of `rotation`) MUST set `recovery: true` on the commit. Knots SHOULD serve both the old head and the recovery head for `RECOVERY_DELAY_SECONDS`.

## Proofs

An inclusion proof for key `k` is the list of MST nodes from the root to the leaf that holds `k`, plus the record block. A verifier:

1. Hashes the record, checks it equals `v`.
2. Reconstructs parent nodes, checks they equal the links.
3. Checks the root equals `commit.data`.
4. Verifies `commit.sig`.

An exclusion proof is the node path showing where `k` would be and that it is not.

Knots advertising `knot.public` MUST implement `tangled.sync.getRecord` returning a proof.

## CAR export

A repository export is a Content Addressable aRchive (CAR) v1 whose roots are `[commit CID]` and whose blocks are: the commit, every MST node, every record, and optionally blobs. The header `roots` MUST be the commit CID.

Partial CAR: blocks needed for a `since` diff (commits from `since` exclusive to head inclusive, plus MST nodes and records that changed).

## Sealed collections in the MST

Sealed records occupy MST keys. The key is `collection + "/" + encrypted_rkey` where `encrypted_rkey` is hex of `ChaCha20-Poly1305(key=HKDF(epoch_secret, "tangled.rkey"), nonce=0, plaintext=rkey)` truncated to 32 bytes and hex-encoded. Listing a sealed collection therefore does not leak plaintext rkeys. Members who hold `epoch_secret[N]` can map keys back. Knots MUST store whatever key the writer sent; they MUST NOT require plaintext rkeys for `vis: sealed`.

Public and `cap` collections use plaintext `collection/rkey`.

## Multiple identities

One knot MAY host many DIDs. Each DID has its own MST and commit chain. There is no knot-level Merkle root.


---

# 08-visibility.md

---
title: Visibility and access control
slug: visibility
order: 8
---

# Visibility and access control

Visibility is a field on the record. It is not a second protocol. Fetch (authorization) and read (confidentiality) are different.

## Classes

### public

- Body is plaintext.
- Anyone MAY fetch. Knots advertising `knot.public` MUST serve public records without a capability.
- Anyone MAY rebroadcast, index, and prove inclusion.
- Looms MAY ingest.

### cap

- Body is plaintext on the knot.
- The knot MUST NOT serve the record, its MST path, or its blobs unless the request presents a valid capability for `repo/read` on that DID, collection prefix, or record CID.
- The knot operator can read plaintext. This class is authorization, not confidentiality. Use it for data the host is allowed to see (server-side search the user opted into, collaborative docs on a trusted knot).
- Looms MUST NOT ingest.

### sealed

- Body is `Ciphertext` (or a header pointing at a ciphertext blob).
- Fetch rules are the same as `cap`: a capability is REQUIRED.
- The knot MUST treat the body as opaque. It MUST NOT log decoded bodies. It cannot decode them without epoch secrets or HPKE recipient keys, which MUST NOT live on the knot except in a client running on the same machine.
- Looms MUST NOT ingest.
- Encrypted rkeys: see [Repositories](./07-repositories.md#sealed-collections-in-the-mst).

## Capability presentation

Requests for `cap` and `sealed` MUST include:

```
Authorization: Cap <base64url(capability-invocation-dag-cbor)>
```

The invocation is specified in [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md). Knots that do not advertise `knot.cap` MUST return `ProfileRequired`.

## What a knot is allowed to know

| Class | Knot sees plaintext body | Knot sees collection and rkey | Knot sees recipients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| public | Yes | Yes | N/A |
| cap | Yes | Yes | N/A |
| sealed | No | Encrypted rkey only | HPKE `enc` bytes, not identities, unless wraps are stored as records the knot can read — wraps are themselves `vis: sealed` |

HPKE wraps of epoch secrets (`sys.circle.wrap`) are `vis: sealed` with `alg = "hpke-record"` to each member. A knot that stores them sees ciphertext. Member identity is in the rkey `{epoch}-{member-base58}` — that leaks membership to the knot. Circle definitions MAY set `hideMembers: true`, in which case wrap rkeys MUST be random TIDs and the member mapping lives inside the ciphertext. Default is `hideMembers: false` because it makes debugging and capability grants tractable. Large-group MLS Welcomes already leak membership to anyone who can fetch the circle log; `hideMembers` is best-effort against the knot, not against members.

## Mixing classes in one repo

A repository MAY contain all three classes. Sync of public collections uses ordinary getRepo. Sync of `cap`/`sealed` collections requires a capability and returns only those collections the capability authorizes. A `repo/read` capability with resource `did:sol:…/pub.tangled.chat` MUST NOT leak sibling collections. A `circle/read` capability MUST return only records whose envelope `circle` matches the resource (plus the circle log on the owner’s repo, as specified in [Circles](./10-circles.md#membership-grant)).

## Blobs

A blob has no `vis` field. Authorization follows records that reference it:

- If at least one **non-deleted** `vis: public` record in that DID’s repository references the blob CID, `tangled.sync.getBlob` MUST serve it without a capability.
- Otherwise the knot MUST require a valid `blob/get` on `tangled://<did>/blob/<cid>`, or a `repo/read` that covers a referencing record, or a `circle/read` that covers a circle-scoped referencing record.
- The same CID referenced from both a public record and a sealed record is public. Clients that need confidentiality MUST AEAD the bytes and store ciphertext.

## Deletes and takedown

Three distinct events. Implementations MUST NOT conflate them.

**Author delete.** A tombstone: same `collection` and `rkey`, `body` `null`, `prev` listing the CIDs being deleted. Public tombstones remain in the MST so sync converges. Sealed deletes MUST be indistinguishable from other sealed records at the knot (same size class); the body ciphertext decrypts to `null`.

**Knot hosting refusal.** A knot MAY stop serving any record (hosting policy). It MUST NOT rewrite a record’s bytes. It MAY omit the record from `getRepo` and MUST answer `getRecord` with `NotFound` or `Unavailable`. This is not a tombstone. Replicas that still hold the commit MAY serve the original bytes after signature verification. Clients MUST NOT treat origin `NotFound` as an author delete when a replica presents a valid inclusion proof for the same head, or when the origin head still includes the key.

**Label.** A signed opinion. It does not delete or authorize refusal. See [Labels](./15-labels.md).

Takedown of public data is hosting refusal, optionally plus a label. Replicas and CAR exports remain valid. This is verifiable exit, not a global delete. Knots MUST still export a CAR of what they do host.


---

# 09-capabilities.md

---
title: Capabilities
slug: capabilities
order: 9
---

# Capabilities

Authorization is object-capability. A capability is a certificate: issuer, audience, command, resource, attenuation, proofs, expiry, signature. Tangled profiles User Controlled Authorization Network (UCAN) semantics and encodes certificates as DAG-CBOR, not JSON Web Tokens (JWT).

## Soundness properties

Implementations MUST provide:

| Property | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Unforgeable | Only the issuer’s Solana key can create a valid certificate at that layer of the chain |
| Monotonic attenuation | A delegate MUST NOT amplify command, resource, or time |
| Revocable | Issuer (or an ancestor) can publish `sys.revocation`; verifiers MUST honor it when online |
| Least authority | Resource is a DID, a collection prefix, or a record CID — not “the knot” |
| Auditable | Certificates are records; they have CIDs |

## Certificate

```
Capability = {
  v: 1,
  iss: did,                 ; issuer
  aud: did,                 ; audience (may be a device did:sol)
  cmd: command,
  res: text,                ; resource URI
  nbf: uint,                ; not-before, Unix seconds
  exp: uint,                ; expiry, Unix seconds
  pol: [* caveat],          ; extra constraints
  prf: [* cid],             ; proofs (parent capabilities)
  ? meta: { * text => any },
  sig: bstr .size 64
}
```

`exp - nbf` MUST NOT exceed `CAPABILITY_MAX_TTL_SECONDS`. `exp` MUST be greater than `nbf`.

The signature uses the Solana off-chain envelope over the unsigned capability map, signed by `iss` (or a device key of `iss` with a proof that allows `cap/issue`).

## Commands

| Command | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `repo/read` | Fetch records and MST nodes |
| `repo/write` | Insert records (still must be signed) |
| `blob/get` | Fetch blobs |
| `blob/put` | Store blobs |
| `circle/invite` | Add members to a circle the resource identifies |
| `circle/remove` | Remove members |
| `circle/read` | Fetch circle-scoped records and referenced blobs; fetch the circle log on the owner repo |
| `knot/replicate` | Pull authorized collections as a replica |
| `cap/issue` | Issue attenuated children |
| `*` | All commands; only the identity key MAY issue `*` |

Unknown commands MUST be rejected.

## Resources

A resource URI:

```
tangled://<did>
tangled://<did>/<collection>
tangled://<did>/<collection>/<rkey>
tangled://<did>/blob/<cid>
tangled://circle/<owner-did>/<circle-rkey>
```

Attenuation: a child capability’s `res` MUST equal the parent’s `res` or be a path prefix extension of it. `tangled://did:sol:X/pub.tangled.chat` is a valid child of `tangled://did:sol:X`. The reverse is invalid.

A `tangled://circle/…` resource is **not** a prefix of `tangled://did:sol:…`. `repo/read` on an author DID does not grant `circle/read`, and `circle/read` does not grant `repo/read` on unrelated collections. `circle/read` authorizes only:

1. `sys.circle` with rkey `<circle-rkey>` on `<owner-did>`
2. `sys.circle.wrap` and `sys.circle.mls` records on `<owner-did>` whose envelope `circle` matches
3. Any record stored by the verifying knot whose envelope `circle` equals `did:sol:<owner>#<circle-rkey>`
4. Blobs referenced by records in (2) or (3)

## Circle/read verification

Verification steps 1–2 and 4–7 of [Invocation](#invocation) apply. Step 3 is replaced: the root `iss` MUST be `<owner-did>` (the author of that `sys.circle` record) or a `cap/issue` delegate recorded in that owner’s `sys/id`. The hosted DID of the knot answering the request NEED NOT equal `iss`. By writing a record with envelope `circle` set, the author delegates fetch authorization for that record to valid `circle/read` capabilities on that circle.

`res` MUST be a `tangled://circle/<owner-did>/<circle-rkey>` URI. A `circle/read` invocation whose `res` is a `tangled://did:sol:…` URI MUST be rejected. A `repo/read` capability MUST NOT authorize `circle/read`, and MUST NOT cause `getRepoAuth` to include sibling collections. Authorization vectors: `spec/vectors/circle-read-auth.json`.

## Caveats

`pol` is a list of predicates. Version 1 predicates:

| Caveat | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `["eq", json-pointer, value]` | Invocation args must equal |
| `["lt", json-pointer, number]` | Less than |
| `["valid_until", seconds]` | Additional cap on `exp` |
| `["max_uses", n]` | Knots that track invocations SHOULD enforce; offline verifiers MAY ignore |

Unknown caveats MUST cause rejection (fail closed).

## Invocation

A request signs an invocation:

```
Invocation = {
  v: 1,
  cap: cid,                 ; leaf capability
  prf: [+ Capability],      ; chain, leaf last, root first
  cmd: command,
  res: text,
  args: { * text => any },
  ts: uint,
  aud: did,                 ; the knot DID, or the resource DID for peer pull
  nonce: bstr .size 16,
  sig: bstr .size 64        ; audience of the leaf cap
}
```

HTTP: `Authorization: Cap <base64url(DAG-CBOR(Invocation))>`.

Verification:

1. Leaf `aud` matches the invocation signer.
2. Each certificate’s `aud` matches the next certificate’s `iss` (or the invocation signer for the leaf).
3. Root `iss` matches the resource DID’s identity (or a `cap/issue` delegate recorded in `sys/id`). For `circle/read`, the resource DID is the circle **owner**, as specified in [Circle/read verification](#circleread-verification).
4. Commands and resources attenuate monotonically.
5. `nbf <= now <= exp` for every certificate.
6. No CID in the chain is present in the issuer’s `sys.revocation` (online) OR every certificate has `exp` within the client’s accepted offline TTL (offline).
7. Signatures verify.

## Revocation

Collection `sys.revocation`, rkey = base32 of the revoked capability CID (without multibase prefix). Body: `{ cid: cid, ts: uint, reason: text }`. Signed by the issuer or an ancestor issuer.

Revocation is not transitive to unrelated chains. It IS transitive to children of the revoked CID: a chain that contains a revoked CID is invalid.

Online verifiers MUST fetch `sys.revocation` for each issuer in the chain (cache TTL RECOMMENDED 60 seconds). Offline verifiers MUST require `exp` no more than 2 hours in the future (`OFFLINE_MAX_REMAINING = 7200`) unless they have a cached revocation MST.

## Root authority

The identity key may issue any command on its DID. It does not need a parent certificate. `prf` is empty. This is the only uncertified issuer.


---

# 10-circles.md

---
title: Circles
slug: circles
order: 10
---

# Circles

A circle is a group. From the user’s point of view the operations are: create, add member, remove member, send, leave. There is no “upgrade group,” no re-invite, no new circle id, no decryption gap, and no prompt. Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) versus Messaging Layer Security (MLS) MUST NOT appear in any client API that authors or readers call.

## Definition record

Collection `sys.circle`, rkey = TID (this TID is the circle id). The author DID plus rkey form the circle DID for resource URIs: `tangled://circle/did:sol:<author>/<rkey>` in prose, stored as `circle: did:sol:…#<rkey>`.

```
Circle = {
  v: 1,
  name: text,
  members: [* did],           ; omitted or empty when hideMembers
  policy: {
    invite: "owner" / "member",
    write: "member",
    history_share: bool,      ; default false
    hideMembers: bool         ; default false
  },
  epoch: uint,                ; current N
  distributor: "hpke" / "mls" / "dual",
  ? mlsGroup: bstr,           ; MLS group context hash, once MLS has been used
  threshold: 16               ; MUST equal CIRCLE_MLS_THRESHOLD
}
```

`distributor` is diagnostic for implementations. Clients MUST NOT show it. `threshold` is written so a reader of the record can detect a non-conforming writer; writers MUST emit `16`.

`sys.circle` MUST use `vis: public` or `vis: cap`. It MUST NOT use `vis: sealed` (policy and membership grants have to be verifiable without the epoch secret). `hideMembers: true` SHOULD use `vis: cap` so looms do not ingest an empty-but-named group if the owner wants it unlisted. Wrap and MLS log records MUST use `vis: sealed` and MUST set envelope `circle`.

## Epoch secret

Application payloads in a circle are AEAD’d with keys derived from `epoch_secret[N]` ([Cryptography](./05-cryptography.md#epoch-application-keys)). How members obtain `N` is the only thing that changes with size.

| Distributor | When (automatic) | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Small-group `hpke` | `len(members) ≤ 16` **and** the circle has never used MLS | HPKE-wrap of `epoch_secret[N]` to each member’s X25519, stored in `sys.circle.wrap` |
| Large-group `mls` | `len(members) > 16`, **or** the circle has already used MLS | MLS exporter secret with label `tangled.epoch` **is** `epoch_secret[N]` |
| Dual-stack `dual` | The single transition after HPKE→MLS grow | Both of the above for epoch `N+1` |

## Write patterns

**Annotation (default).** A member writes a `vis: sealed` record in **their** repository with envelope `circle` set, `body.alg = "epoch-aead"`, `epoch = N`, `ref` optional. The record is portable. The circle knot does not become a god. Other members fetch it with a **membership grant** (`circle/read`), not with pairwise `repo/read` on every sender. Cost: each member pulls every other member (N−1).

**Shared repo.** The circle has a dedicated Solana key (a DID the owner creates) whose repository is the shared object. Used for wikis, datasets, and optional high-traffic chat. One subscribe. Specified below.

Both patterns use the same epoch secret. Users do not pick a pattern as a cryptographic mode; clients pick it per application.

## Membership grant

When a DID is added to a circle, the owner MUST issue a capability to that DID:

- `cmd`: `circle/read`
- `res`: `tangled://circle/<owner-did>/<circle-rkey>`
- `exp` within `CAPABILITY_MAX_TTL_SECONDS`

This is the **membership grant**. The adder MAY also issue `circle/invite` if `policy.invite` is `"member"`. Application senders MUST set envelope `circle` on circle-scoped records. Knots that advertise `knot.group` or `knot.sealed` MUST honor `circle/read` as specified in [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md#circleread-verification).

On remove or leave, the owner MUST publish `sys.revocation` for that member’s membership grant(s) **and** advance the epoch. Revocation stops fetch; the epoch advance stops read of new payloads. A revoked member MAY still hold ciphertext they already fetched and old epoch secrets.

## Shared-repo pattern

The owner creates a Solana keypair whose DID `W` owns the MST. `W` is hosted on a knot. Records in that repo have `author` = `W`. Collaborators hold attenuated `repo/read`, `repo/write`, and `blob/*` capabilities; they sign records with their device key (`signedBy` + `proof`). The hosting knot MUST sign commits with a key of `W` (identity key or a device key with `repo/write`). That is the same hosting arrangement as any identity that does not keep its identity key on the knot.

`vis: cap` is the class for a wiki the host is allowed to search. `vis: sealed` plus envelope `circle` is the class for a confidential shared object. Collaborators cannot rotate `W`; the owner holds that key. Example collection: `pub.tangled.page`, rkey = slug.

The owner MAY instead host the wiki as a collection prefix on their own Decentralized Identifier (DID). Then `author` is the owner, and collaborators are device-like writers of that collection. A dedicated DID isolates a compromised collaborator capability from the owner’s other collections.

## Create

Owner generates `epoch_secret[0]` (32 cryptographically random bytes), writes `Circle` with `distributor: "hpke"`, `epoch: 0`, `members: [owner]`, and a wrap to the owner. MLS is not involved.

## Add member

User action: add a DID.

Implementation:

1. Authorize via `circle/invite` policy.
2. Linearize on the circle commit log (one membership change at a time).
3. Issue (or refresh) the membership grant to the new member.
4. If `distributor` is `hpke` and `len(members)+1 ≤ 16`: new epoch `N+1`, new random `epoch_secret[N+1]`, HPKE-wrap to every current member including the new one. Old wraps remain so history decrypts.
5. If `distributor` is `hpke` and `len(members)+1 > 16`: perform **seamless grow** below. This is still “add member” to the user.
6. If `distributor` is `mls` or `dual`: MLS Add + Commit, Welcome for the new member. If `dual`, also HPKE-wrap `epoch_secret[N+1]` to members who have not processed Welcome.

If `history_share` is true, the owner (or the adder, if they hold old secrets) additionally wraps epoch secrets `0..N` to the new member. If false, the new member cannot decrypt pre-join records. `history_share` is an explicit policy, not a side effect of size migration.

## Seamless grow (HPKE → MLS)

The `addMember` that first exceeds 16 members MUST:

1. Create an MLS group whose members are exactly the current circle including the new member. Credential for each member is that member’s 32-byte Solana public key. Ciphersuite `0x0001`.
2. Publish a Welcome for every current member as `sys.circle.mls` records, `vis: sealed` to that member (HPKE 1:1). Offline members pick them up on next sync. No accept dialog.
3. Advance to epoch `N+1`. Set `epoch_secret[N+1]` to the MLS exporter secret (label `tangled.epoch`, context `uint64be(N+1)`, 32 bytes).
4. Set `distributor: "dual"`. HPKE-wrap `epoch_secret[N+1]` to every member who has not been observed to process Welcome (initially: everyone). Application senders encrypt **once**, to the epoch AEAD key. Laggards decrypt via the wrap they already understand; caught-up members decrypt via MLS.
5. Dual-stack ends when every member known at the transition has a Welcome receipt record (`sys.circle.mls` body `{type:"receipt", epoch, member}`) **or** `DUAL_STACK_MAX_SKEW_EPOCHS` epochs have passed **or** `DUAL_STACK_MAX_SKEW_SECONDS` have elapsed, whichever first. Then `distributor: "mls"`. Knots MUST stop writing new HPKE wraps for this circle except as required by `hideMembers` debugging flags (none in v1).
6. Membership changes during dual-stack are applied as MLS epochs, never as a new HPKE-only epoch.

## Never downgrade

Once a circle has published an MLS epoch (`mlsGroup` is set), it stays on MLS even if membership later drops to two. Implementations MUST NOT return to `hpke`. Ping-pong is not seamless. MLS is correct for two members.

## Agreement rotation

Rotating `sys/id.agreement` (with or without rotating `pubkey`) changes the X25519 key that Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) wraps and Messaging Layer Security (MLS) leaves use. Moving a knot does **not**. Rotating only a device key does **not**. HPKE versus MLS MUST NOT appear as a user-facing “upgrade group,” “re-wrap,” or “re-invite” prompt. The rotating member’s client performs the steps in this section automatically after it publishes the new `sys/id`.

### Who initiates

The rotating member’s client MUST initiate re-wrap. Other members (usually the circle owner, on the next epoch advance) MUST read the current `agreement` from that member’s `sys/id` when wrapping. They MUST NOT wait for a confirmation dialog.

### MUST path

After a new `sys/id` whose `agreement` changed:

1. The rotating client MUST HPKE-wrap every `epoch_secret[N]` it still needs — the current epoch, and prior epochs if it retains history or `history_share` is true — to the **new** agreement key. Info string remains `tangled.hpke.epoch.v1`.
2. It MUST publish those wraps as `sys.circle.wrap` records with envelope `circle` set and `vis: sealed`. It SHOULD write them in **its own** repository so its other devices can pull without `repo/write` on the owner. The owner SHOULD copy observed self-wraps into the owner’s circle log.
3. If `distributor` is `mls` or `dual`, the rotating client MUST publish an MLS Update/Commit whose leaf HPKE key is the new agreement public key. If `pubkey` also changed, the MLS credential MUST be the new 32-byte Solana public key. Offline circle members pick this up from the log; it is not a re-invite.
4. The rotating client SHOULD `tangled.sync.notify` the circle owner’s knot after the new `sys/id` commit.

Identity-key rotation without a new `agreement` is forbidden: writers MUST emit a new X25519 key together with a new `pubkey` ([Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md#rotation)).

### Old agreement window

Wraps to the previous agreement key remain valid for decryption until `AGREEMENT_ROTATION_MAX_SKEW_SECONDS` after the new `sys/id` record’s `ts`. During that window:

- Devices of the rotating member that have not synced MAY decrypt with the old agreement private key.
- An owner who advances the epoch SHOULD wrap to **both** agreement keys if it has not observed a wrap (or MLS receipt) for the new key.
- After the window, owners MUST wrap only to the current `sys/id.agreement`. The rotating client SHOULD discard the old agreement private key once every device it controls holds the new wraps.

An offline **device of the rotator** that returns after the window without new wraps MUST obtain them from another of that member’s devices (the online device re-publishes). An offline **circle member** is unaffected except that they will observe the new `sys/id` on next pull.

### Device-key-only rotation

Revoke the old device’s capabilities; issue new ones to the new device key. `sys/id.pubkey` and `sys/id.agreement` MUST NOT change. Clients MUST NOT re-wrap epoch secrets and MUST NOT publish MLS Updates solely because a device key changed.

## Remove member and leave

User action: remove or leave.

Advance epoch. Under `hpke`, generate a new secret and wrap to remaining members only. Under `mls` or `dual`, MLS Remove + Commit. The removed member loses `epoch_secret[N+1]` onward (forward secrecy). They keep secrets they already have. There is no extra “key rotation ceremony” in the UI.

## Send

Encrypt the application body with the current epoch AEAD. Recipients decrypt with `epoch_secret[epoch]` from wraps or MLS. If a sender is lagging (still on `N-1` during dual-stack), receivers MUST accept epochs in `[current - DUAL_STACK_MAX_SKEW_EPOCHS, current]`. Older epochs MUST be rejected for new sends; they remain valid for historical records.

Senders using the annotation pattern MUST set envelope `circle`. Clients SHOULD `subscribe` or poll each current member’s knot; they MAY `tangled.sync.notify` after send. There is no circle-wide inbox POST.

## Offline members

Welcomes and wraps are records. Sync delivers them. An offline member who returns during dual-stack reads via HPKE wrap, processes Welcome, and continues on MLS. An offline member who returns after dual-stack MUST still have a Welcome in the log; if the Welcome was GC’d (MUST NOT before max-skew), the member is re-Welcomed by any current member — still not a user-facing re-invite: the client does it on sync.

## Forced-upgrade denial of service

Spam-adding members to trigger MLS is a policy problem, not a dialog. Circles SHOULD rate-limit invites (`max_adds_per_hour` in `policy`, default 30). Clients MUST NOT ask the user to “confirm MLS.”

## Conformance
