`spec/vectors/circle-grow-dual-stack.json` MUST pass: 16 members on HPKE, 17th added, one member offline throughout, pre-migration records still decrypt, circle id unchanged, no client API flag. Shrink 20→5 stays MLS. Add and remove during dual-stack linearize. Agreement rotation MUST follow [Agreement rotation](#agreement-rotation); `spec/vectors/circle-read-auth.json` covers membership-grant authorization, not wrap ciphertext.


---

# 11-sync.md

---
title: Synchronization
slug: sync
order: 11
---

# Synchronization

Followers pull. Authors do not push into N inboxes. Relays are not the source of truth. The source of truth is a signed commit CID (the **head**) and the Merkle Search Tree (MST) behind it.

## Head

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.getHead?did=`

Returns `{ did, commit, rev, knot }`. `commit` is the head CID. No capability for public repos. `repo/read` required if the knot hides the DID (unusual; default is to advertise heads).

Clients MUST cache `(did, commit)` and detect rollback: a head with `rev` less than a previously verified `rev` for the same DID is an attack or a recovery race. Recovery races are specified in [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md#rotation).

## Get record

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.getRecord?did=&collection=&rkey=`

Returns the record block, the MST inclusion proof, and the commit. For `vis: cap` and `vis: sealed`, a capability is REQUIRED. For sealed collections the caller MAY pass `rkey` as the encrypted key they computed.

## Get blocks

`POST /xrpc/tangled.sync.getBlocks` with body `{ cids: [cid] }` (max 256). Returns a CAR of those blocks. Missing CIDs are listed in `missing`.

Version 1 uses a **single MST**. Public collections are served without a capability. When walking a proof for a public record, interior nodes MAY mention sibling keys, including encrypted rkeys of sealed records. Sibling keys leak the existence of other records; that is acceptable. Sibling values are CIDs; fetching a non-public record CID still requires a capability. Proof nodes themselves are not confidential. Knots MUST serve MST nodes for public proofs without a capability, even if siblings are sealed keys.

`getBlocks` of a non-public **record** CID requires a capability that covers that record (`repo/read`, or `circle/read` if the record is circle-scoped). `getBlocks` of a **blob** CID MUST follow the same authorization as `getBlob`.

## Get blob

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.getBlob?did=&cid=`

Returns raw bytes (`Content-Type: application/octet-stream`) whose BLAKE3-256 matches the CID (codec `raw` 0x55). Authorization is specified in [Visibility](./08-visibility.md#blobs): serve without a capability only if a non-deleted public record in that DID’s repository references the CID; otherwise require `blob/get`, `repo/read` covering a referencing record, or `circle/read` covering a circle-scoped referencing record.

Knots advertising `knot.public` MUST implement this method for publicly referenced blobs. Authorization vectors: `spec/vectors/getblob-auth.json`.

## Get repo

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.getRepo?did=&since=`

Returns a CAR. Without `since`, the full public repo (commit, public MST, public records). With `since` (a commit CID), a diff. Blobs are not included unless `blobs=true`.

Authorized variant: `POST /xrpc/tangled.sync.getRepoAuth` with invocation, returns authorized collections. If the invocation command is `circle/read`, the CAR MUST include only records the capability authorizes (circle-scoped records on this DID, plus the circle log when this DID is the owner) and MUST NOT include sibling collections.

## Notify (optional)

`POST /xrpc/tangled.sync.notify` body `{ did, commit }` — a hint that a head moved. Knots MAY ignore. Used by replicas and looms. MUST NOT be required for correctness.

## Live

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.subscribe?did=&collection=` Upgrade: WebSocket.

Messages: `{ t: "commit", commit: cid, ops: [{action, collection, rkey, cid}] }`.

Public collections: no cap. Others: cap on subscribe. Heartbeat every 30 seconds. The server MAY drop slow clients.

## Query backlinks

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.queryBacklinks?cid=`

Optional `collection=` (restrict hits) and `limit=` (default 50, max 500).

Returns public records **this knot already stores** whose envelope `ref` equals `cid`, or whose application body `reply` equals `cid` when envelope `ref` is absent. This is a **local backlink index**, not a network search.

```
{
  "hits": [{ "did", "collection", "rkey", "cid", "commit" }],
  "count": 3,
  "overlay": true,
  "complete": false
}
```

Knots advertising `knot.public` SHOULD maintain the index from public records they ingest (hosted repositories, follows, replicas). They MUST NOT crawl other knots in order to answer this method. They MUST NOT include `vis: cap` or `vis: sealed` records. Tombstones MUST NOT appear in `hits`. `count` is `len(hits)` after those filters (or the untruncated count if `limit` clipped `hits`). `overlay` MUST be `true`. `complete` MUST be `false` unless the knot can prove it stores every public annotator (v1 knots cannot; they MUST send `false`).

A knot that does not implement the index MUST return `MethodNotImplemented`. Clients treat that as zero observed remote annotations from this knot.

Discovery of annotations without knowing every annotator DID is specified in [Looms](./14-looms.md#annotation-discovery).

## Follow

A follow is a public record `tangled.graph.follow`. The follower’s client:

1. Resolves the target DID to a knot URL.
2. Pulls `getHead` / `getRepo` on an interval or subscribe.
3. Stores the knot URL in local follow state.

The author’s knot does no extra work per follower. That is the efficiency claim against ActivityPub.

## Replication

A replica holds a copy of a repo. Public repos: anyone MAY replicate. `cap`/`sealed`: `knot/replicate` capability. Replicas advertise themselves in their own `sys/id` or in a loom. Clients MAY fail over to a replica if the author’s knot is down, after verifying the commit signature.

## Diff cost

MST diff is O(changed keys × tree height). Tree height is ~log16(n). This is the efficiency claim against Nostr’s “replay all events from all relays.”


---

# 12-http-api.md

---
title: HTTP API
slug: http-api
order: 12
---

# HTTP API

Knots speak HTTP. Method names follow `tangled.<ns>.<name>`. The path is `/xrpc/<method>`. GET for cacheable reads, POST for bodies and invocations that do not fit a query string.

Machine-readable: [`spec/http/openapi.yaml`](./http/openapi.yaml).

## Content negotiation

Clients MUST send `Accept: application/cbor, application/json`. Knots MUST serve `application/cbor` (DAG-CBOR) when requested, and MAY serve `application/json` using the IPLD JSON mapping. `Content-Type` on POST MUST be one of those two.

CIDs in query strings are multibase base32 (`b…`).

## Errors

JSON/CBOR map:

```
{ "error": "CapabilityRequired", "message": "…", "retry": false }
```

| error | HTTP | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `InvalidRequest` | 400 | Bad params |
| `InvalidSignature` | 400 | Sig verify failed |
| `CapabilityRequired` | 401 | Missing cap |
| `CapabilityInvalid` | 403 | Cap present but fails |
| `NotFound` | 404 | No such DID/record |
| `MethodNotImplemented` | 404 | Unknown `tangled.*` method on a Tangled knot |
| `ProfileRequired` | 501 | Method needs a profile the knot omitted |
| `BlobTooLarge` | 413 | |
| `RateLimited` | 429 | |
| `Unavailable` | 503 | |

## Methods

### tangled.node.describe

`GET`. No auth. Returns profiles, protocols, maxBlob, knot DID.

### tangled.sync.getHead

`GET ?did=`. See [Synchronization](./11-sync.md).

### tangled.sync.getRecord

`GET ?did=&collection=&rkey=`. Optional `Authorization: Cap`.

### tangled.sync.getBlob

`GET ?did=&cid=`. Raw blob bytes. No capability when a live public record references `cid`; otherwise `Authorization: Cap` (`blob/get`, `repo/read`, or `circle/read`). See [Synchronization](./11-sync.md#get-blob).

### tangled.sync.getBlocks

`POST` `{ "cids": ["b…"] }`.

### tangled.sync.getRepo

`GET ?did=&since=&blobs=`.

### tangled.sync.getRepoAuth

`POST` invocation + `{ did, since, blobs }`. For `circle/read`, the CAR is only circle-scoped records (and the circle log on the owner).

### tangled.sync.queryBacklinks

`GET ?cid=&collection=&limit=`. Local public backlink index. Knots SHOULD implement it; they MUST NOT crawl. See [Synchronization](./11-sync.md#query-backlinks).

### tangled.sync.notify

`POST` `{ did, commit }`.

### tangled.sync.subscribe

`GET` WebSocket.

### tangled.repo.putRecord

`POST` `{ record }` plus either identity session (SIWS cookie, knot-local) or `repo/write` capability. The knot MUST verify the record signature and MUST NOT accept a record whose `author` the caller cannot speak for.

### tangled.repo.putBlob

`POST` raw bytes, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`. Returns `{ cid }`.

### tangled.repo.import

`POST` a CAR (`Content-Type: application/vnd.ipld.car`) plus identity session or `repo/write` on the DID. The knot MUST verify every commit signature in the CAR and MUST refuse a DID it already hosts unless `force` is true (recovery).

### tangled.identity.resolve

`GET ?handle=` or `?did=`. Returns DID, `sys/id` CID, knot endpoints. The knot MAY resolve handles it does not host by performing DNS/SNS lookup.

### tangled.cap.verify

`POST` an Invocation. Returns `{ ok: true, cmd, res }` or `CapabilityInvalid`. Useful for gateways.

### tangled.loom.query

`GET ?q=&type=`. OPTIONAL. Looms only. When `type=ref`, `q` is a record CID. Response includes `hits`, untrusted `count`, `overlay: true`, `complete: false`. See [Looms](./14-looms.md).

### tangled.loom.firehose

`GET` WebSocket of public commits. OPTIONAL. Looms only.

## Sessions (SIWS)

Sign In With Solana authenticates a browser to **this knot** for `putRecord` as the identity. The SIWS message MUST include the knot domain, the DID, a nonce, and `issuedAt`. Sessions MUST expire (RECOMMENDED 24 hours). SIWS MUST NOT replace record signatures: the record is still signed with the off-chain envelope. A knot MAY hold a delegated device key and sign on behalf of a web client only if the user issued a `repo/write` capability to that device key; that is an implementation choice and MUST be disclosed in `node.describe` as `custodialSign: true`. Default is `false`.

## CORS

Public reads MUST be CORS-available (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`). Authorized methods MUST NOT use `*`; they MUST echo a specific origin or use a non-browser client.

## Transport

Production knots MUST use HTTPS. `localhost` MAY use HTTP. HTTP/2 is RECOMMENDED.


---

# 13-resolution.md

---
title: Resolution
slug: resolution
order: 13
---

# Resolution

Resolution turns a handle or a DID into a knot URL and a DID document. It does not confer trust beyond what signatures later verify.

## DID → knot

1. If the client has a cached `sys/id` for the DID, use `endpoints` whose `type` is `"knot"`, in list order, skipping endpoints that failed recently.
2. Else if an on-chain `did:sol` document exists and lists a service endpoint of type `TangledKnot`, use it. On-chain data is OPTIONAL.
3. Else the client MUST be given a knot URL out of band (QR, follow record that includes `knot`, previous session).

There is no global directory. That is intentional.

## Handle → DID (DNS)

Hostname `h`.

1. Query TXT `_tangled.h`. If a TXT value starts with `did:sol:`, that is the DID. If a TXT value starts with `head=`, it is a commit CID hint.
2. If TXT is absent, `GET https://h/.well-known/tangled-did` (Follow redirects only to the same host). Body is the DID (trimmed) or JSON `{"did":"…","head":"b…"}`.
3. Fetch `sys/id` from the knot in that DID’s endpoints (or from a well-known `https://h/.well-known/tangled-id.json` serving the record).
4. Verify `h` is in `alsoKnownAs`. If not, abort.

TXT and well-known MUST agree if both exist; if they disagree, abort.

## Handle → DID (SNS)

Let `n` be an SNS domain.

1. Resolve the SNS record per the Solana Name Service program for the cluster implied by the DID (mainnet default).
2. The record MUST contain a field `tangled` or, if absent, the account owner MUST equal the identity public key.
3. Fetch `sys/id`, verify `n` is in `alsoKnownAs`.

SNS seizure: whoever controls the SNS domain controls the handle, not the DID. Same as DNS.

## Bidirectional rule

Clients MUST reject handle claims that fail either direction. A DID listing a handle it does not control is a lie. A handle pointing at a DID that does not list it is a lie.

## Head hints

DNS TXT `head=<cid>` and SNS `head` reduce stale-head windows. Clients SHOULD fetch the hinted commit and verify it is a descendant of (or equal to) their cache, or a valid rotation/recovery.

## Negative caching

Failed DNS lookups SHOULD be cached per DNS TTL. Failed well-known lookups SHOULD be cached 5 minutes. Clients MUST NOT cache a successful DID→knot mapping longer than 24 hours without re-checking `sys/id`.


---

# 14-looms.md

---
title: Looms
slug: looms
order: 14
---

# Looms

A loom indexes **public** heads. It is an unprivileged overlay. Two knots can sync without one. A client that never talks to a loom can still follow people it knows.

## What a loom does

- Subscribe to or poll `getHead` on knots it knows.
- Ingest public records (and only public records).
- Serve queries: posts mentioning a DID, recent public commits, records whose envelope `ref` or body `reply` equals a CID, hashtag indexes if applications emit them.
- Serve labels it trusts, or pass through labeler DIDs.

## What a loom MUST NOT do

- Require membership for a knot to exist.
- Ingest `vis: cap` or `vis: sealed` records.
- Rewrite records. Indexes point at CIDs.
- Claim to be authoritative for a DID’s head. The author’s knot (and signed commits) are authoritative.

## Discovery of knots

A loom learns knot URLs from:

- Operator configuration
- `tangled.sync.notify`
- Public follow graphs (walk `tangled.graph.follow`, resolve handles)
- Other looms (gossip of `{did, knot, commit}` tuples)

There is no required global firehose. A loom MAY offer one for public data: a WebSocket of public commits. Clients treat it as a hint stream and MUST verify signatures.

## Client composition

Clients SHOULD let the user pick looms, as they pick labelers. A censored loom is left. That is verifiable exit at the discovery layer.

## Node advertisement

A loom is a knot with `profiles` containing `loom.index`. Methods:

- `GET /xrpc/tangled.loom.query?q=&type=`
- `GET /xrpc/tangled.loom.firehose` WebSocket of public commits

These methods are OPTIONAL. They are specified so looms interoperate instead of inventing search APIs.

`tangled.loom.query` returns `{ hits, count, overlay, complete }` for public records only. Each hit is `{ did, collection, rkey, cid, commit }`. When `type=ref`, `q` is a record CID; hits MUST be public records whose envelope `ref` equals `q`, or whose body `reply` equals `q` when envelope `ref` is absent. Looms MUST NOT invent hits for `cap` or `sealed` records.

`count` is the number of distinct matching record CIDs the loom observes (not clipped by a hit page size). `overlay` MUST be `true`. `complete` MUST be `false` in v1 (a loom is not the whole network). Comment counts are specified below.

## Annotation discovery

There is no global reply inbox and no ActivityPub (AP) inbox fan-out. A reader finds annotations on a record by **pulling indexes of records already stored**, never by contacting every annotator Decentralized Identifier (DID).

Version 1 path, in order:

1. **Author repo.** Pull the target author’s repository. Annotations the author wrote (same DID) are visible. Remote annotations are not, unless they happen to live in that repo.
2. **Local backlink index.** `tangled.sync.queryBacklinks?cid=` on knots the client already talks to (the author’s knot, the client’s home knot, replicas). Each knot answers only from public records it already stores. Specified in [Synchronization](./11-sync.md#query-backlinks).
3. **Loom overlay (OPTIONAL).** `tangled.loom.query?type=ref&q=<cid>` on looms the user chose. Looms remain optional: a client that only pulls the article author’s repo MUST still work; it sees zero remote annotations until it consults an index.

Clients MUST union hits by record CID and MUST verify each hit’s signature and MST inclusion before display. Clients MUST NOT treat an empty result as proof that no annotations exist in the network.

Knots SHOULD index `ref` / `reply` as they ingest public records. They MUST NOT start a new pull of unknown DIDs because of a `queryBacklinks` call (that would restore N²).

## Comment counts

A comment **count** is an untrusted overlay. It MUST NOT be a field on the target record that clients treat as canonical: the target author can write any integer, and no reader can verify it without enumerating annotations.

**Computation.** For a target CID `T` and an observer (client, knot, or loom):

```
count(T) = number of distinct public, non-deleted record CIDs
           this observer stores whose envelope ref = T
           (or body reply = T when ref is absent)
```

Typical filter: collection `pub.tangled.annotation` or posts with `reply`. Observers MAY filter further (block lists, labels). They MUST document the filter if they expose `count`.

**Labeling.** Clients MUST present the figure as an overlay bound to its source, for example `12 (this loom)` or `3 (observed locally)`. They MUST NOT present it as an author-signed or globally complete count. `overlay: true` on the query response is the machine label.

Hostile looms can inflate or omit counts. Clients that care MUST verify hits or pick another loom. That is the same trust model as any loom query.


---

# 15-labels.md

---
title: Labels
slug: labels
order: 15
---

# Labels

Moderation is signed opinion, not protocol-level deletion. A **label** is a public record asserting something about a DID or a record CID. Clients subscribe to **labeler** DIDs and apply labels locally. Knots MAY additionally refuse to host (that is hosting policy, not a label).

## Record

Collection `tangled.label`, rkey = TID.

```
Label = {
  v: 1,
  src: did,                 ; labeler, MUST equal author
  uri: text,                ; tangled://did/… or tangled://did/collection/rkey
  val: text,                ; "spam", "nsfw", "scam", "ok", or a namespaced value
  neg: bool,                ; true = retract
  ts: uint
}
```

`val` SHOULD be a short token. Namespaced values (`pub.example.hate`) are allowed. Clients MUST ignore unknown `val` they have no policy for.

## Semantics

- The labeler DID is the authority over its own labels, nothing else.
- A later label with `neg: true` and the same `(src, uri, val)` retracts.
- Labels do not delete data. They advise clients.
- Multiple labelers may disagree. Clients MUST expose composition: which labelers are on.

## Knots

A knot MAY refuse to serve content it will not host. It MUST NOT rewrite. It MAY attach its own labels. It MUST still export a CAR of what it does host.

A knot MUST NOT silently drop public records from `getRepo` **because a labeler disliked them**. Filtering by label is a client (or loom) job. Hosting refusal is a different event: `NotFound` or `Unavailable` for that record, optional omission from `getRepo`, which replicas can fill. Author tombstones are a third event. See [Visibility](./08-visibility.md#deletes-and-takedown).

Clients that fail over to a replica MUST verify the commit signature and MUST NOT treat origin unavailability as a tombstone.

## Comparison

This is AT Protocol’s label idea, kept, without making an AppView mandatory to see the network. ActivityPub instance-admin god-mode is a knot hosting policy, not a network-wide fact. Nostr client-side mute lists are a subset of labels.


---

# 16-interoperability.md

---
title: Interoperability
slug: interoperability
order: 16
---

# Interoperability

Tangled is a substrate that other networks can bind to. Bridges MUST follow this chapter so they round-trip with each other instead of each inventing a mapping.

## Foreign identity bindings

Collection `sys.binding`, rkey = TID.

```
Binding = {
  v: 1,
  tangled: did,             ; did:sol:…
  protocol: "nostr" / "atproto" / "activitypub" / "farcaster",
  foreign: text,            ; npub/hex, AT DID, actor URI, or FID string
  nonce: bstr .size 16,
  ts: uint,
  attested: bool,           ; true only for activitypub
  foreignSig: bstr,         ; protocol-specific
  ? foreignProof: any
}
```

The Tangled record signature proves the Solana key. `foreignSig` proves the foreign key (or host). Both MUST verify. `sys/id.bindings` SHOULD list the CID.

### Nostr

`foreign` is the 64-hex public key. `foreignSig` is a Schnorr signature (BIP-340) over SHA-256 of the UTF-8 string:

```
tangled-binding:v1:did:sol:<base58>:<hex(nonce)>
```

Alternatively, `foreignProof` MAY be a NIP-01 event of kind `30078` (arbitrary app data) with `content` equal to the Tangled DID and `tags` including `["d","tangled-binding"]`. Then `foreignSig` is that event’s `sig`. Verifiers MUST check `pubkey` equals `foreign`.

### AT Protocol

`foreign` is the AT DID (`did:plc:…` or `did:web:…`). `foreignProof` MUST include the DID document. `foreignSig` is the AT signing key’s signature over the same `tangled-binding:v1:…` bytes, using the AT key type (k256 or p256 as in the DID document). Verifiers MUST check the signing key is listed in that document.

### ActivityPub

ActivityPub actors do not have a user key in the ratified specification. `attested` MUST be `true`. `foreign` is the actor URI. `foreignProof` is either:

- An HTTP Message Signature over `GET {actorURI}` that includes header `Tangled-Binding: did:sol:…`, or
- `https://{actor-host}/.well-known/tangled-binding.json` listing `{ "did": "did:sol:…", "actor": "https://…" }` served on the actor host.

Clients MUST display AP-bound identities as **host-attested**, never as key-equals-person.

### Farcaster

`foreign` is the FID decimal string. `foreignSig` is Ed25519 from a currently valid Farcaster signer key over `tangled-binding:v1:…`. `foreignProof` MUST include the signer key and a proof it is registered to the FID (hub message or on-chain lookup description).

## Envelopes

Collection `sys.foreign`, rkey derived as in [Idempotent import](#idempotent-import).

```
Foreign = {
  v: 1,
  protocol: text,           ; MUST be "nostr" / "atproto" / "activitypub" / "farcaster"
  foreign_id: text,         ; canonical id, see below
  bytes_cid: cid,           ; raw blob of original bytes
  translator: did,          ; gateway DID
  attested: bool,
  ? mapped: cid             ; CID of the Tangled application record, if any
  ? mapped_lossy: bool
}
```

**Round-trip:** exporting a previously imported object MUST emit the original bytes from `bytes_cid` when present. Gateways MUST NOT re-encode Nostr events or AT records if `bytes_cid` exists.

## Canonical foreign_id

`foreign_id` MUST be the **canonical** identifier of the foreign object, not a gateway-local alias. Two gateways importing the same object MUST produce the same `(protocol, foreign_id)` pair.

| `protocol` | Canonical `foreign_id` |
| --- | --- |
| `nostr` | Lowercase 64-hex NIP-01 event id (SHA-256 of the serialized event) |
| `atproto` | Strong AT URI: `at://<did>/<collection>/<rkey>#<record-cid>` with the DID, collection, rkey, and record Content Identifier (CID) as in the AT commit. The `#<record-cid>` fragment is REQUIRED so an edit is a new object |
| `activitypub` | The object’s `id` Internationalized Resource Identifier (IRI), exactly as published, as an absolute IRI. Gateways MUST NOT invent a fragment or trailing slash. Scheme `http` / `https` MUST be lowercase; the rest of the IRI MUST be copied verbatim |
| `farcaster` | Lowercase hex of the Farcaster message hash |

Unknown `protocol` values MAY be imported; then `foreign_id` MUST be a stable, documented identifier for that protocol. Gateways that speak the four listed protocols MUST use this table.

## Idempotent import

The rkey of `sys.foreign` MUST be the lowercase hex of BLAKE3-256(`UTF-8(protocol) || 0x00 || UTF-8(foreign_id)`) where `foreign_id` is the canonical value. A second import of the same `(protocol, foreign_id)` MUST update that record in place (`prev` pointing at the prior envelope CID) and MUST NOT insert a second envelope. If the computed rkey already holds an envelope whose stored `foreign_id` differs, that is a hash collision: the knot MUST NOT overwrite; it MUST reject the write.

If `mapped` is set and that CID is still in the local MST as a native application record, a later import MUST NOT write a second application record.

**Native export.** Exporting a Tangled-authored object MUST write `sys.foreign` with `mapped` equal to the native record CID and `bytes_cid` equal to the bytes that were actually sent. `foreign_id` MUST be the canonical id of those bytes (for example the Nostr event id after the event is signed). A later export of the same native CID MUST reuse that envelope and MUST emit `bytes_cid`; it MUST NOT mint a new foreign id. If the native record has a new CID (an edit), the gateway MAY create a new envelope with a new canonical `foreign_id`.

`mapped_lossy: true` MUST be set on the envelope when the gateway also writes a Tangled application record and the mapping truncates or stubs.

## Duplicate envelopes (pre-canonical or divergent gateways)

If two envelopes for the same object were written with different `foreign_id`s (gateways that ignored this chapter, or a protocol that had no canonical id yet), clients MUST detect duplicates as follows, in order:

1. **`bytes_cid` equality.** Distinct `sys.foreign` records whose `bytes_cid` values are equal are the same object. Clients MUST render one and MAY keep both envelopes.
2. **Id inside the bytes.** If `bytes_cid` differs (re-encoding) but the foreign bytes contain a protocol id, clients MUST extract it with the table above (Nostr event id from the event, AT record CID from the commit proof, ActivityPub `id` IRI from the JSON-LD, Farcaster message hash) and compare canonical `(protocol, foreign_id)`.
3. **`mapped` equality.** Distinct envelopes with the same `mapped` CID are the same native record exported twice.

Clients MUST NOT treat distinct canonical `foreign_id`s as duplicates without one of these equalities. Merging duplicate envelopes (one surviving rkey, the other tombstoned with `prev`) is OPTIONAL operator hygiene.

## Translation tables

Normative tables live in `spec/interop/*.yaml`. Summary:

| Tangled | ActivityPub | Nostr | AT Protocol |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pub.tangled.post` | `Note` | kind `1` | `app.bsky.feed.post` |
| `pub.tangled.article` | `Article` | kind `30023` (NIP-23) | `app.bsky.feed.post` with long text, or a custom lexicon — **lossy** |
| `pub.tangled.annotation` | `Note` (`inReplyTo`) | kind `1` (`e` tag) | `app.bsky.feed.post` (`reply`) — **lossy** |
| `tangled.graph.follow` | `Follow` | kind `3` contact list (NIP-02) / NIP-51 | `app.bsky.graph.follow` |
| `tangled.graph.block` | `Block` | NIP-51 mute/block | `app.bsky.graph.block` |
| `vis: sealed` | stub `Note` content `"(encrypted)"` or omit | MUST NOT export plaintext | MUST NOT export plaintext |

Lossy mappings MUST set `mapped_lossy: true` on the envelope when a gateway also writes a Tangled application record.

## Gateway knots

A knot MAY speak foreign protocols. It advertises them in `tangled.node.describe` → `protocols`.

### ActivityPub

C2S/S2S facade over the local repo. Outbox items are public Tangled posts mapped to `Note`. Inbox items become `sys.foreign` plus, if mappable, a `pub.tangled.post` with `attested: true`. The gateway DID is `translator`. Dual-publish (a native public post also emitted as an outbox `Note`) MUST still write the envelope; if that `Note` returns on S2S, idempotent rkey collision MUST update the envelope only.

### Nostr

A NIP-01 relay interface. `EVENT` of kind 1 with a valid sig becomes an envelope + mapped post, `attested: false`. `REQ` filters are served from public collections. Sealed records MUST NOT appear.

### AT Protocol

Subset: `com.atproto.repo.getRecord`, `com.atproto.repo.listRecords`, `com.atproto.sync.getRepo` over public collections whose schemas have an AT lexicon mapping. The MST is the same MST. This is a facade, not an AT PDS.

## Honesty

| Foreign protocol | Import authenticity |
| --- | --- |
| Nostr | Independently verifiable (event id + sig) |
| AT Protocol | Independently verifiable (record + commit proof) if the gateway stored the proof |
| ActivityPub | Gateway-attested |
| Farcaster | Independently verifiable if signer proof is stored |

Clients MUST surface `attested` in UI when rendering imported AP objects.


---

# 17-migration.md

---
title: Migration and multi-device
slug: migration
order: 17
---

# Migration and multi-device

Account portability is a CAR plus a DID. The knot is a location.

## Export

`GET /xrpc/tangled.sync.getRepo?did=&blobs=true` with a `repo/read` capability covering all collections (identity session suffices on the home knot). The CAR MUST include commits, MST nodes, records of every visibility class the capability allows, and referenced blobs.

The operator SHOULD also export device capability private keys they still need, out of band. The CAR does not contain private keys.

## Import

On the destination knot:

1. `POST /xrpc/tangled.repo.import` with the CAR (method defined in OpenAPI). The knot verifies commit signatures.
2. Write a new `sys/id` with the new knot in `endpoints` (first).
3. Sign a new commit (rotation commit if `pubkey` also changes; otherwise a location-only commit signed by the identity key).
4. Update DNS TXT / well-known / SNS to the same DID (handle unchanged) and optional `head=` hint.

Followers pull the new endpoint from `sys/id`. There is no follower-move protocol. Old knots MAY 301 `getHead` to the new URL.

## Multi-device

Each device gets a device key and a `repo/write` capability with a TTL. Revoke by `sys.revocation`. The identity key stays on a hardware wallet or an offline machine.

Web clients: either the browser holds a device key in non-extractable WebCrypto, or the knot custodially signs (`custodialSign: true`, disclosed). Custodial signing means that knot can write as the user. It is OPTIONAL and NOT RECOMMENDED for sealed circles.

## Backup

Any replica with `knot/replicate` is a backup. The operator MAY copy the SQLite file; that is an implementation convenience, not a protocol object.

## Circle membership across move

Circle Welcomes and membership grants are addressed to DIDs, not knots. Moving the knot does not change membership. The member’s client still decrypts. If `history_share` was false, old epochs remain as they were. Device-key revocation (`sys.revocation` of a `repo/write` capability) does not remove the DID from circles; other devices of the same DID continue.

Moving a knot MUST NOT rotate the identity or agreement keys. Location is `sys/id.endpoints`.

If the operator **also** rotates the identity key and/or the X25519 `agreement` key, that is [Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md#rotation) plus [Circles](./10-circles.md#agreement-rotation): the rotating member’s client MUST re-wrap circle epoch secrets to the new agreement key (Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) wraps and, when the distributor is Messaging Layer Security (MLS), an MLS Update/Commit). That MUST NOT be presented as a user-facing cryptographic mode. Old agreement wraps remain valid for `AGREEMENT_ROTATION_MAX_SKEW_SECONDS`. Device-key-only rotation MUST NOT re-wrap.

The old knot MAY retain sealed ciphertext until the operator deletes it. Copies that already left do not come back. That is not fixed by changing `endpoints`.

## What does not migrate automatically

- Loom indexes (they recrawl)
- SIWS sessions on the old knot
- Gateway-attested AP follower counts on foreign servers (those servers follow the actor URI, which a gateway may keep stable)


---

# 18-threat-model.md

---
title: Threat model
slug: threat-model
order: 18
---

# Threat model

Assumptions: Ed25519, BLAKE3, HPKE, and MLS are as specified in their RFCs. Attackers include malicious knots, stolen wallets, leaked capabilities, hostile looms, hostile gateways, DNS/SNS operators, and other members of a circle.

## Identity

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Steal identity key | Rotation keys; hardware wallet; device keys for daily use | If rotation keys are stolen too, the attacker is the identity |
| Steal device key | Capability TTL and revocation | Offline verifiers may accept until TTL |
| Hostile knot serves stale `sys/id` | Cached CID, DNS/SNS `head=` hint, replicas | First-time clients with only a knot URL can be lied to until they compare a second source |
| PLC-style directory seizure | No PLC | None of that class |
| DNS or SNS handle seizure | DID remains; handle moves | Users who only know the handle can be phished |

## Signatures

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Confuse a record sig with a Solana transaction | Mandatory `\xffsolana offchain` envelope | Implementations that skip the envelope are non-conforming and unsafe |
| Replay an invocation | `nonce` + `ts` on Invocation; knots SHOULD track nonces | Distributed knots need shared nonce state or short clock skew |

## Visibility

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Knot reads `vis: cap` | Expected; do not put secrets in `cap` | Operator compromise |
| Knot reads `sealed` | Epoch secrets and HPKE recipient keys MUST NOT live on the knot | Client malware; knot that is also the client |
| Listing sealed collections leaks rkeys | Encrypted rkeys | Existence of sealed records and, if `hideMembers` is false, wrap rkeys leak membership to the knot |
| Dual-stack window: HPKE wrap of the new epoch secret lives too long | `DUAL_STACK_MAX_SKEW_*`; stop wraps after | An offline member’s wrap can be fetched by anyone with a leftover `repo/read` cap during the window |
| Agreement rotation: leftover wrap to the old X25519 key | `AGREEMENT_ROTATION_MAX_SKEW_SECONDS`; wrap to both keys only during the window; rotating client discards the old agreement private key after | Offline device of the rotator that misses the window needs a republish from another of their devices |

## Circles

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Removed member reads new messages | New epoch; they are not wrapped; MLS Remove | They keep old epoch secrets |
| Compromised member | They can read current epoch; MLS updates after remove | Past messages they already decrypted |
| MLS epoch skip / fork | Linearize on circle commit log; verify MLS epoch is monotonic | Split-brain if two owners ignore linearization — policy `invite: owner` avoids dual owners |
| Forced-upgrade DoS (spam adds to trigger MLS) | `max_adds_per_hour`; not a user dialog | Determined owner can still grow |
| Stolen or leftover membership grant | Revoke on remove; epoch advance | Fetch of ciphertext until revocation is visible; decrypt still needs epoch secrets |
| Malicious Welcome | Verify credential = member Solana key; ignore Welcomes not in the circle log signed by an authorized committer | None if clients skip verification |
| Identity/agreement rotation without re-wrap | Rotating member’s client MUST re-wrap and MLS-Update; not a user prompt | Offline rotator device past max-skew cannot decrypt until republish |

## Discovery and gateways

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loom omits you | Choose another loom; pull direct | Reach among people who only use that loom |
| Loom or knot inflates a comment count | Counts are untrusted overlays (`overlay: true`); clients MUST label the source and MAY verify hits | Users who treat a count as canonical |
| Gateway forges ActivityPub | `attested: true` in UI; no author sig exists to check | Users who ignore the badge |
| Gateway drops `bytes_cid` and re-encodes | Spec forbids; clients SHOULD prefer envelopes with `bytes_cid` | Non-conforming gateways |
| Two gateways assign different `foreign_id`s | Canonical `foreign_id` per protocol; rkey MUST be BLAKE3 of `protocol`, a 0x00 byte, and `foreign_id`; duplicates detected by `bytes_cid` or id-inside-bytes | Envelopes written before canonicalization remain until merged |
| Selective translation | Another gateway; original network remains | Split view |

## Availability

| Attack | Control | Residual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Knot downtime | Replicas, CAR export, client cache | If nobody replicated and the operator has no CAR, data is gone |
| Blob withholding | CID mismatch detected; replica | Same as knot downtime for those bytes |

## Out of scope

- Traffic analysis of who pulls which DID (use Tor or equivalent if needed)
- Quantum break of Ed25519/X25519 (future version)
- Legal compulsion of a knot operator (sealed records still hide bodies; metadata may not)


---

# 19-comparison.md

---
title: Comparison
slug: comparison
order: 19
---

# Comparison

This chapter is evidence-based. Claims about other protocols cite their own specs and widely documented behavior. Tangled does not win “every dimension including network effects”; it has no incumbent graph. That is stated here so marketing cannot creep in.

## Identity

| Dimension | Nostr | AT Protocol | ActivityPub | Farcaster | Tangled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Primitive | secp256k1 key | DID (`did:plc` default) | `https` actor URI | On-chain FID | Solana Ed25519 key, `did:sol` generative |
| Rotation | Not in NIP-01 | Rotation keys + PLC log | Change servers, new URI | Custody key transfer | Rotation keys in `sys/id`; optional on-chain `did:sol` |
| Recovery | None | 72h window via PLC | Admin | Recovery address | Recovery keys in `sys/id`, 72h delay |
| Handle | NIP-05 | DNS | `@user@host` | Fname / ENS | DNS and SNS, bidirectional |
| Who seizes the account | Nobody (and nobody restores) | Not the DID; PDS can takedown | Home-server admin | Recovery address; Fname registry | Nobody for the DID; DNS/SNS for the handle |
| Cost to exist | Free | Free | Free (operator pays) | Gas + rent | Free; Solana rent only if persisting `did:sol` on-chain |

Nostr NIP-01: the public key is the account; lost `nsec` is permanent. AT Protocol `did:plc`: a global directory (Bluesky-operated at time of writing) is the default method. ActivityPub: identity is the actor URI on a domain. Farcaster SPEC: FID on OP Mainnet, recurring storage rent.

## Data and sync

| Dimension | Nostr | AT Protocol | ActivityPub | Farcaster | Tangled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Store | Relays, events | PDS repo (MST) | Server collections | Hubs / Snapchain CRDT | Knot repo (MST) |
| Sync | Subscribe to events | Firehose + pull | Inbox POST | Gossip CRDT | Pull MST; optional loom firehose of **public** heads |
| Self-host cost | Cheap relay | Cheap PDS, expensive relay/AppView | Full server | Hub | Cheap knot; loom optional |
| Portability | Rebroadcast events | CAR + DID | Followers, not posts (Mastodon) | FID transfer | CAR + DID |

Mastodon’s own move docs: posts do not move. AT Protocol repository spec: CAR export. ActivityPub delivery: POST to inboxes (N²). AT Protocol federation architecture: relays aggregate PDS firehoses.

## Access control and confidentiality

| Dimension | Nostr | AT Protocol | ActivityPub | Farcaster | Tangled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authorization | Relay policy; otherwise public | Public repo; permissioned-data proposal is a **second** protocol, “access control, not confidentiality” | Addressing (`to`/`cc`/`bto`), often ignored | Public hubs | Capabilities on the **same** repo |
| Confidentiality | NIP-44 DMs | Out of scope in permissioned-data proposal | Not E2EE | Not E2EE | `vis: sealed` + HPKE and MLS |
| Groups | Relays / NIP-29 | Spaces (proposal) | Groups as actors | Channels | Circles; size migration invisible |

AT Protocol proposal 0016 (permissioned data): quote, “this protocol provides access control, not confidentiality.” Tangled refuses that split.

## Discovery and moderation

| Dimension | Nostr | AT Protocol | ActivityPub | Farcaster | Tangled |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Global index | Many relays, hope | Relay + AppView, de facto required to see the network | Instance timelines | Hubs | Loom optional |
| Moderation | Client mute, relay ban | Labels + AppView | Instance admin | App-edge | Labels; knot hosting policy |

## Interoperability

Nostr, AT Protocol, and ActivityPub do not specify round-tripping each other. Tangled specifies bindings, envelopes with original bytes, and translation tables. ActivityPub imports remain attested because the AP spec has no author signature.

## Where Tangled is not better

- **Network effects.** Zero users at spec time.
- **Implementation maturity.** This document is a spec, not a running network.
- **Human onboarding without keys.** ActivityPub email-and-password on a server is easier. Tangled can custodially sign (`custodialSign`), at the cost of knot trust.
- **Private global search.** Impossible if sealed; AT Protocol permissioned-data also refuses this, honestly.
- **Handle independence from DNS/SNS.** Zooko’s triangle. Same class of problem as everyone else.

## Summary sentence

Tangled takes Nostr’s key-as-account, AT Protocol’s signed Merkle repo and labels, ActivityPub’s self-hosting, and none of their fused mistakes: un-rotatable keys, a required global directory or firehose, server-custodial identity, or access control without confidentiality.


---

# 20-use-cases.md

---
title: Use cases
slug: use-cases
order: 20
---

# Use cases

This chapter is **informative**. It walks applications through Tangled version 1 so an implementer can see which records, visibility classes, capabilities, and sync calls are involved. Normative requirements live in the cited chapters. Where a walkthrough needed a protocol rule that was missing, that rule was added there. Acronyms are defined in [Terminology](./01-terminology.md); the first use of each in this chapter is expanded.

Actors are named. Identifiers are abbreviated (`did:sol:A…`). There is no live network.

## 1. Public microblog

**Actors.** Ada self-hosts a `knot.public`. Bo follows Ada. Cyd labels Ada’s post. A loom is optional.

**Records.** Ada writes `pub.tangled.post` (`vis: public`, `text`, optional `media` blob Content Identifiers (CIDs), optional `reply` = parent **record CID**). Bo writes `tangled.graph.follow` (`vis: public`, rkey = Ada’s Decentralized Identifier (DID)-safe, body `subject`, optional `knot` URL). Cyd writes `tangled.label` (`vis: public`) with `uri` `tangled://did:sol:A…/pub.tangled.post/<rkey>` and `val` `spam` or `ok`.

**Vis / caps.** None for public fetch. Device key + `repo/write` if Ada’s identity key is offline ([Identifiers](./04-identifiers.md#device-keys)).

**Sync.** Bo resolves Ada (handle or follow.`knot`), `getHead` / `getRepo` or `subscribe` on Ada’s knot. Replies live in the **replier’s** repo; they are not POSTed into Ada. Thread assembly is: walk `reply` / `ref` CIDs; query knots Bo already talks to (`tangled.sync.queryBacklinks?cid=`); and/or query a loom (`type=ref`). Ada never fans out.

**Failure / threat.** Loom omits Ada: Bo still pulls Ada’s knot. Cyd’s label does not delete the post ([Labels](./15-labels.md)). Ada’s knot can refuse to host; that is not a network delete (use case 8). A client that only pulls Ada sees Ada’s own replies; remote annotations appear after consulting a backlink index. Empty index is not proof that none exist ([Looms](./14-looms.md#annotation-discovery)).

**Coverage.** `reply` is a record CID. Discovery is pull-based: author repo, local backlink index, optional loom. There is no global inbox; that is a protocol limitation with specified client behavior, not an unspecified gap.

## 2. Private circle chat (5 → 20)

**Actors.** Owner O, members M1–M19. M19 is offline during the add that crosses 16. `history_share: false`. Users add members; they never pick a cryptographic distributor.

**Records.** O writes `sys.circle` (`vis: public` or `vis: cap`, never `sealed`) with `policy.history_share = false`. Wraps and Welcomes: `sys.circle.wrap` / `sys.circle.mls`, `vis: sealed`, envelope `circle` set. Each send is `pub.tangled.chat` in the **sender’s** repo, `vis: sealed`, `alg: epoch-aead`, envelope `circle` = `did:sol:O…#<circle-rkey>`. On add, O issues a **membership grant**: `circle/read` on `tangled://circle/did:sol:O…/<rkey>` to the new member ([Circles](./10-circles.md#membership-grant), [Capabilities](./09-capabilities.md)).

**Vis / caps.** Fetch: `circle/read` (cross-repo) or `repo/read` on the sender. Read: `epoch_secret[N]`. The hosting knot sees ciphertext and, unless `hideMembers`, wrap rkeys.

**Sync.** Members list peers from `sys.circle`, resolve each `sys/id`, `getRepoAuth` / `subscribe` with `circle/read`. Annotation pattern: N−1 pulls. Crossing 16 is still “add member”: same circle id, dual-stack epoch, Welcomes in the log. M19 returns, reads via wrap, processes Welcome, continues. Pre-join records do not decrypt (`history_share` false). Shrink 20→5 stays on the large-group distributor ([Circles](./10-circles.md#never-downgrade)).

**Failure / threat.** Removed member keeps old epochs, loses new ones. Forced adds are rate-limited, not a confirm dialog. Offline past dual-stack max-skew: client re-Welcomes on sync; not a user-facing re-invite. Honest loss: membership grants must be revoked on remove or the removed member can still **fetch** ciphertext they can no longer decrypt.

**Coverage.** Size migration was specified. Missing pieces were envelope `circle`, `circle/read`, and how members fetch each other’s annotation-pattern messages.

## 3. Long-form publishing with media and comments

**Actors.** Ada publishes. Bo comments. Media on Ada’s knot.

**Records.** Ada `putBlob` for the article body (markdown) and for images. Ada writes `pub.tangled.media` (`blob`, `mime`, `alt`) and `pub.tangled.article` (`title`, `blob` canonical body, optional `text` preview, `media` CIDs). Bo writes `pub.tangled.annotation` in Bo’s repo with envelope `ref` = article CID.

**Vis / caps.** Public article: anyone `getRecord` / `getBlob`. Capability-gated draft: `vis: cap` until Ada writes a public successor (`prev`).

**Sync.** Readers pull Ada. Comments: pull Bo if known; `tangled.sync.queryBacklinks?cid=<article>` on knots already in use; optional loom `type=ref&q=<article-cid>`. Counts from those queries are overlays (`overlay: true`), never a field Ada can forge as canonical ([Looms](./14-looms.md#comment-counts)). Blobs via `tangled.sync.getBlob` ([Synchronization](./11-sync.md#get-blob)).

**Failure / threat.** Ada tombstones the article; blob becomes non-public once no live public record references it. Bo’s annotation remains in Bo’s repo (dangling `ref` is allowed). A client that never consults an index sees zero remote comments; that is required behavior, not a bug.

**Coverage.** Article schema, `pub.tangled.annotation`, `ref`, `getBlob`, backlink query, overlay counts.

## 4. Shared wiki / dataset (shared-repo)

**Actors.** Owner O creates circle DID `did:sol:W…` (dedicated key) hosted on O’s knot. Collaborators C1, C2.

**Records.** Circle definition as in use case 2. Wiki pages: `pub.tangled.page` in **W’s** Merkle Search Tree (MST), rkey = slug (`Home`, `rfc.draft` displayed as `rfc/draft`). Dataset rows: application collection plus blobs. Concurrent edits: **Last-ts-wins among causal heads**; a record whose `prev` lists both concurrent heads is a merge record ([Data model](./06-data-model.md#merge-rule-last-ts-wins)). Slugs MUST NOT contain `/`; `.` is the nested-page separator ([Data model](./06-data-model.md#page-slugs)).

**Vis / caps.** Typical wiki: `vis: cap` (host may search). Confidential wiki: `vis: sealed` + envelope `circle` + epoch Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD). O issues to each collaborator: `repo/read` + `repo/write` + `blob/*` attenuated to `tangled://did:sol:W…/pub.tangled.page` (and blob prefix), plus `circle/read` if sealed. Writers sign records with their device key; `author` is `did:sol:W…`; `signedBy` + `proof` required. The knot signs **commits** with a device key of W ([Circles](./10-circles.md#shared-repo-pattern)).

**Sync.** One `subscribe` on W. Not N member pulls.

**Failure / threat.** `vis: cap` means O’s knot operator can read plaintext — that is the point of this class. Stolen collaborator cap: revoke, epoch-advance if sealed. The circle identity key is another secret O must hold; collaborators cannot rotate W.

**Coverage.** Shared-repo pattern, commit signing, `author`/`signedBy`, page schema, Last-ts-wins, nested slugs. No Conflict-free Replicated Data Type (CRDT).

## 5. Cross-network import, export, dual-publish

**Actors.** Gateway G (`gateway.nostr` + `gateway.ap`). Ada bound to a Nostr key (verifiable) and an ActivityPub (AP) actor (attested).

**Records.** `sys.binding` for each foreign id. Import: blob of original bytes; `sys.foreign` with canonical `foreign_id` (Nostr event id, AT strong URI, ActivityPub object `id` Internationalized Resource Identifier (IRI), Farcaster message hash), `bytes_cid`, `translator` = G, `attested` false for Nostr and true for AP; optional mapped `pub.tangled.post`. rkey of `sys.foreign` MUST be hex of BLAKE3 (`protocol || 0x00 || canonical foreign_id`) ([Interoperability](./16-interoperability.md#canonical-foreign_id)).

**Round-trip.** Export MUST emit `bytes_cid` bytes when present. Native Ada post exported to Nostr: G writes `sys.foreign` with `mapped` = Ada’s post CID and `bytes_cid` = the event bytes. Re-export of that CID MUST reuse the envelope and MUST NOT mint a new event id. Re-import MUST NOT create a second post. If two gateways used different `foreign_id`s before canonicalization, clients detect duplicates by `bytes_cid` equality or the protocol id inside the bytes.

**Dual-publish.** Ada’s public post is mapped to an AP `Note` in G’s outbox. If that `Note` returns on Server-to-Server (S2S), the idempotent envelope key collides and G updates the envelope, not the native record.

**Failure / threat.** Clients MUST show AP objects as host-attested. G can lie about AP; G cannot forge a Nostr sig if the client verifies. AP follower counts live on foreign servers; article→Authenticated Transfer Protocol (ATProto) is lossy (`mapped_lossy`).

**Coverage.** Bindings, envelopes, attested vs verifiable, canonical `foreign_id`, idempotent rkeys, native-export `mapped`, duplicate detection.

## 6. Account migration

**Actors.** Ada moves from knot K1 to K2. Same DID, same handle. Laptop device key revoked. Circle member throughout.

**Records.** Export a Content Addressable aRchive (CAR) (`getRepo?blobs=true` with a cap covering all classes). `import` on K2. New `sys/id` with K2 first in `endpoints`. Location commit (identity key). Domain Name System (DNS) / Solana Name Service (SNS) unchanged for the DID; update knot URL / `head=` hint. `sys.revocation` for the laptop capability.

**Vis / caps.** Identity session on K2. Membership grants are to Ada’s DID, not K1; circle membership survives ([Migration](./17-migration.md)). Device revoke does not remove Ada from circles.

**Sync.** Followers re-resolve `sys/id` (max 24h cache). K1 MAY 301 `getHead`. No follower-move protocol.

**Failure / threat.** Sign In With Solana (SIWS) on K1 dies. Looms recrawl. K1 may still hold sealed ciphertext until the operator deletes it; copies that left K1 remain. If nobody replicated and the CAR is lost, data is gone. **Location move does not rotate keys.** If Ada also rotates the identity and agreement keys, her client MUST re-wrap circle epoch secrets to the new X25519 `agreement` key (and MLS-Update if the circle is on MLS) without a user-facing mode ([Circles](./10-circles.md#agreement-rotation), [Migration](./17-migration.md#circle-membership-across-move)). Device-key-only revoke of the laptop does not re-wrap.

**Coverage.** Location vs identity rotation vs device rotation are distinct. Foreign AP followers follow G’s actor URI, not K1.

## 7. Sealed media album (invented)

**Actors.** Ada shares an album with circle C (use case 2), not with the public.

**Records.** For each photo: AEAD the bytes under `epoch_secret[N]`; `putBlob` the ciphertext; `pub.tangled.media` with `vis: sealed`, envelope `circle`, `Ciphertext` header `{alg: epoch-aead, epoch: N, blob: cid}` (`ct` omitted). Album index: `pub.tangled.album` (`title`, `items` = media record CIDs), same vis and `circle`.

**Vis / caps.** `circle/read` + `blob/get` (implied by `circle/read` for referenced blobs). Knot MUST NOT serve these blobs as public. Clients MUST encrypt media bytes; a plaintext blob CID in a sealed body is fetchable by anyone who learns the CID from a leak.

**Sync.** Members pull Ada (and other contributors) as in use case 2; `getBlob` per item.

**Failure / threat.** `history_share: false`: a late joiner does not decrypt old photos. Removed member keeps photos they already fetched. Same CID placed in a **public** record makes the bytes public. Honest loss: encrypted rkeys hide names, not the count of sealed objects on the knot.

**Coverage.** Ciphertext-as-blob existed; `getBlob` authorization and the album schema did not.

## 8. Takedown versus replica (invented)

**Actors.** Ada’s public post. Knot K refuses to keep hosting it (policy). Replica R still has the CAR. Labeler L writes `val: nsfw`.

**Records.** Three different objects, not one:

| Event | What the MST does | What clients see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Author delete | Tombstone (`body` `null`, `prev` set) | Protocol delete; sync converges |
| Knot hosting refusal | Bytes unchanged if retained; MAY omit from `getRepo` | `NotFound` or `Unavailable`; **not** a tombstone |
| Label | New `tangled.label` | Opinion; compose labelers |

**Sync.** Clients that only talk to K lose availability. Clients that fail over to R, after verifying commit signatures, still see the post unless Ada tombstoned it. K MUST NOT rewrite record bytes.

**Failure / threat.** Users confuse K’s 404 with Ada’s delete. Hostile K withholds; replicas detect by head/rev, not by filling missing records as “deleted.” Honest loss: there is no global takedown.

**Coverage.** Visibility and labels said this in outline; the three-way distinction and replica failover were easy to misread.
